This, unlike the third game, is a very well done PC port. I played it a long time ago and just noticed I forgot to recommend it!
+ the graphics are quite awesome considering the system requirements aren't set that high
+ the combat (flow): Out of all Devil May Cry games I've played, this one has the second best flowing combat (right after DMC3). If you played DMC4 you probably remember that some enemies were really badly designed: either extremely annoying to beat in a group or designed to only be attackable when they show a weakness, which takes away from combat flow. Do you remember? Well, good news and bad news: it's not as bad as it was in DMC4, but it still is restrictive in this edition of the game for some enemies that can only be attacked by a specific type of weapon. In the definitive edition of this game they changed this but, alas, definitive edition is not available on PC. ♥♥♥♥ me, right? I'm still giving the game a plus for this because they improved it from DMC4. It's really not bad.
+ the combat (animations): really nothing to criticize here. Dante tears the enemies apart with an elegance and smoothness I've not seen before in this series. I like the combat animations very much.
+ the combat (ease of use): the combat is user friendly. Very minor weapon spoilers here, it shouldn't ruin your experience but I'm putting a spoiler tag anyway:
. There are not THAT many combos for each weapon but you can combo one weapon into another (by switching weapon DURING a combo), allowing for more combo depth.
+/- The story is not that exciting
+/- The depth/personality of the characters is okay/meh, depending on taste.
- Combat depth, a minor point for me. I know I mentioned above in a POSITIVE point that the combat is easy to learn and easier to master than in, say, DMC4 (Dante) or DMC3. But while I don't care about this much, they simplified the combat somewhat by taking things like style switching away which raised the skill ceiling by a lot. Again, it's not that much of a negative point for me, but it objectively reduces combat depth somewhat so I only find it fair to mention it here.
- Combat controls. Most of them feel fine, but I had an issue with two of them on my Xbox360 pad. One was the special gun move for which you have to press A and X at the same time, and the second the devil trigger for which you have to press both L3 and R3 at the same time. Half of the time I wouldn't press them at the exact same time leading to me failing to do what I was intending to do and instead doing some other move that messes the combat up. Instead of using one of the shoulder buttons for, say, the special gun move, BOTH shoulder buttons actually have the same function...WHY!? You CAN rebind those moves, so it is not a problem for me anymore BUT: for some reason, you cannot rebind the devil trigger key in the ingame config. You have to do it manually in the config file, and I see no reason for this to be necessary. Minor negative point for inconvenience.
- I'm not a fan of the devil trigger mechanic. It is powerful, yes, but I don't like it. Basically, you use it less often than in other DMC since it takes longer to charge, but it about doubles your damage and makes all (non-boss) enemies unable to act or defend themselves. It should feel powerful, yes, but DMC3/4 had plenty powerful devil triggers that still wouldn't save you from getting beaten up if you perform badly.
- I like the cheeky Dante from the other parts in the series more. This one is more rebellious and more of a "♥♥♥♥ you" guy than the cheeky, taunting Dante I know.

In a world of mundain arcade like racing games with unrealistic controls, sloppy physics and horrendous AI, F1 2012 is a light in the dark. My first impression on this game was like many who look at racing titles with a unenthused "Meh". However, after devoting time to it, you'll easily see how great this title is. Whether you're using a controller or you're a hardcore sim racer using a steering wheel, you're find many hours of enjoyment in this.
First and foremost, the graphics are stellar. If you have a machine which can handle the graphics, crank it up. You'll be blown away by the level of detail. Next for me is obviously the gameplay. You genuinely get the "race car driver" feeling as you race in search of that extra .1 second you know that you can take off of your qualifying time. You race to get your team on top, your name on top and to come out on top. You also feel like you're part of a team as your crew chief/engineer gives you track data as it pertains to you. If you've never played a racing title before, you may find the learning curve of the racing terminology to be pretty steep. You'll have to learn about KERS, DRS, prime tires, optimal tires, intermediate tires, wet tires, when to use them and also about fuel mixes which can help you save fuel by using less of it (at the cost of speed) or use more fuel which makes you go faster. All of which play into your general lap time and track position.
One of the best things I love about this game is the AI. They're smart. They don't try to run you off the road but they're aggressive just like F1 drivers are. If you leave a gap on your inside before a turn, they'll slide in and take it. However, when you're coming up on lap traffic, they'll slow down and pull to the other side of the track to let you pass. You can really get into some close racing action on here. The one and only downside I can see is the difficulty level. It's hard to find a middle ground sometimes as you can find yourself running away from the field or find the field running away from you. The gap between Intermediate and Professional is quite large. In Intermediate you may qualify 1-2 seconds faster than the next car whereas in Professional you may find yourself 2-4 seconds off the pace. But, there's a lot of ways to get faster and they all involve playing the game and simply getting better at it!
All in all, this a great game which I would recommend to anyone looking to have some close racing action.
Easily an A+ in my books!

I recently finished Batman : Arkham Origins. Always been a huge fan of the Arkham series and this game did not disappoint! I played it for around 12.5 hours, completed the story and most of the side quests (aside from Enigma and the escaped inmates)
It's definitely a solid game and I personally feel it deserves 7.5/10. It was well worth the 9.98$ I spent (the game and its season pass cost me 4.99$ each), couldn't be happier! Thank Gaben for Steam Sales! That being said, I doubt I would be this cheerful had I paid the full price for the game and the season pass (19.99$ each).
As you all know, no game is perfect and there were a few things that bugged me. Of course, there were also some positive points about this very successful game by WB Games Montréal, so let's talk about them. Starting with the good stuff.
*Boss fights - each boss fight felt unique and intense. The devs impressed me in this category. These fights were fun and left me wanting for more.
*Setting - What can I say? It's always fun to glide around Gotham City in the middle of winter, looking for thugs to beat up and serve some sweet justice.
*Story & Dialogue - They did a very good job in this department, plus the cut scenes were really good. I especially enjoyed how well Batman and Alfred worked together. The butler's banter and affection for Bruce adds a little something to the game.
*Fast Travel - Nice little addition to the series, after playing the game for hours and hours, you may want to skip gliding across districts and just take the Batwing.
*Solving Crimes -  The crimes are one of the highlights of the game. The Bat is the world's greatest detective so it's always a pleasure watching him work.
Now to list some of the small complaints I've got....
*A longer story - I could not help myself from wanting more! I think I finished the main story in just 8 or 9 hours. Would be great if the story was just a little bit longer.
*I badly wanted to wear other suits but I had to finish the main story first! That was not the case in Arkham City as the developers released the cheat codes. Wish they would have done something similar for Origins.
*I noticed only policemen, thugs and victims were out on the streets. I wish there were more people that I can see and interact with. I think the reason that they were indoors was because of a curfew but I wanted to see more people in Gotham. Maybe a girl is being mugged and I get to save her. An old couple walking in the park and suddenly there are thugs who want to cause trouble. Batman just so happens to be around and saves the day. Something like that.
Again, they're all very minor and I am happy with the game. Thank you to everyone involved in making this game! I highly recommend it! Looking back, I still feel that there was not enough time between Origins and Arkham City to make any revolutionary changes...in other words, not enough innovation but I can't deny that it is a damn good game.

Ori and the Blind Forest is a fantastic example of putting love and care into your product. From start to finish, Ori is a captivating, fun, and moving adventure. This is a must play for anyone who enjoys the "Metroid-vania" style of games.
PROS:
-Tight, fluid gameplay and level design
-Fantastic visuals
-Beautiful, moving, and dynamic soundtrack
-One of the single best progression systems I've experienced in a "Metroid-vania" style game
-Lots of hidden areas and secrets to find!
-A heartfelt and, at times, heartbreaking story
-Difficulty that rarely feels unfair, and rightfully challenges the player's skill and understanding of the game
-Great deal of variety between "levels", from lush forests, to a fiery mountain, and an icey cavern
CONS:
-Several frustrating "trial and error" moments, though few and far between
-Relatively short game, depending on your skill level
The greatest parts of Ori are the level design, sense of progression through upgrading movement and attacking abilities, and the astounding soundtrack.
The game does have a few moments of frustration stemming from small sections that I felt were more "trial and error" rather than testing your skill at the game, however these are few and far between and take almost nothing away from the game at the end of the day.
Honestly, I found it very difficult to come up with legitimate cons to Ori and the Blind Forest. I first experienced the game as I received it for free with the purchase of an Xbox One several years ago, however I never got very far as I rarely touch consoles these days. Years later, I decided to sit down and play through the game on Steam as I've owned it for a long time. Little did I know that I would experience what I can now safely say is one of my favorite gaming experiences of all time. I played and beat the original release of Ori in just two or three sittings, then proceeded to purchase the Definitive Edition re-release and, once again, played and completed the game 100% on hard difficulty.
All in all, Ori and the Blind Forest is a game I could possibly call a masterpiece.
What are you doing reading these reviews, anyway? Buy this game!  Support Moon Studios!

I purchased Prison Architect when it was still in Alpha development quite some time ago - however I never played it.  I believe it was on a Summer Sale or something at the time and it was too good of a price to pass out.
Jump to recently, armed with a new PC I decided to try out some of the games I had "collected" during my time with my old PC and gave it a whirl.  Now with over 56 hours played, I have to say that this is a FUN game.  Is it perfect?  No.   Could it be better?  Of course.  Does it still have bugs?  Apparently.
It doesn't take long to understand what to do (the mini-campaign does a fantastic job of teaching you the basics while telling a heart-pulling story).   The info bubbles in-game do a good job at explaining the requirements for certain things, and the wiki (accessible through the menu) fills in the gaps of the rest.  Sometimes it can be frustrating to get your prisoners to want to do something and other times you'd think it would be fun to suddenly have a riot from your normally calm prisoners, but either way, I just can't stop playing.
I'm not sure how much more development this game will see (and I hope there is a bit) but the modding community at least exists should I wish to experience more.  Now I'm not sure if I ever would have enjoyed paying full retail for this game, but at a Steam Sale price, it is really worth the price!

Super Meat Boy is a platformer controller-destruction simulator created by the gods at Team Meat. The game consist of Meat Boy going hell and back for her girlfriend Bandage Girl, because "he can't live without her". Although, Dr. Fetus hates Meat Boy so he decides to kidnap Bandage Girl and going on a endless chase so that Meat Boy dies over and over again.
The levels consist of a lot of death of which Meat Boy has to dodge to get to the end of the level, marked as Bandage Girl.
Meat Boy traverses the levels at extreme speeds, while jumping and wall-jumping to reach his lover. Although, all the levels are a threat. Spikes, sawblades, cliffs, spinning sawblades, lava, demon dogs, salt, bloodclots and more are after (sometimes just waiting really) Meat Boy and his meaty legs. The levels are amazingly designed, always having a easy solution to beat, just requiring practice in skill. Almost all levels have a dark world variant, being even harder.
There are extra levels like Warp Zones, having 8/16-bit graphics, and some having special guests from other games, such as Commander Video, Flywrench, and... The Kid *shivers*. There are also "glitch" levels, having the same sort of graphics, but having special conditions needed to be met to be entered.
There's not much i can say about this game. It's a perfect masterpiece that needs to be played by everyone. You can't go wrong with this game. Good luck.

Rust Review 2017
By: James H.
Rust is a fantastic base building, survival, mutiplayer game. It's great to play with your friends and solo. Although, I highly recommend playing Rust with a group of friends and create funny moments together.
Pros++
1, Fantastic, refined crafting/base building system:
If you ever played Minecraft you're pretty much familiar with how Rust's crafting/base building system is like. For crafting you'll need components then the blueprints and BOOM you have what you want. Everything feels smooth and user friendly.
2. Strategic Raiding gameplay:
A big aspect of Rust is the gameplay mechanic of "raiding". In order to obtain valuable items such as: guns, raw resources, ammo; one must either craft and grind or raid bases to obtain them. In order to raid you'll require a solid team and communication for the raid to be successful. This gameplay aspect not only changes the tone of the game (carefree, relaxing basebuilding and farming resources) to a tactile Rainbow Six Seige gameplay atmosphere.
3. Constant updates:
Rust updates are not only frequent but they are constantly creating new changes that will make the game even better to experience. The developers seek to find better implementations through community feedback. Fresh new weapons, items, gameplay mechanics are all present within each new update.
4. Visually Stunning
Rust is a gorgeous game. Through its dynamic lightings, detailed textures, and vibrant color pallettes, it allows the players to immerse themselves in a beautiful virtual world.
Cons--
1. Optimization Issues
Rust is a early access game, meaning it will run poorly due to optimization. Even high end PC's run into framerate issues, and constant stutering. This can all affect the gameplay which can take you out of the immersion.
2. Hackers
You'll find yourself running into a situation where a player has headshotted you from an almost impossible situation. You find asking yourself, "Is he hacking or am I bad?", that is the ultimate question in life. But in all honestly, I've ran into blantantly obvious hackers. They exist, and at the time of this review, I can confidentally say that Facepunch has been doing a great job at suppressing them as of late.
All in all, I find myself playing rust more than I would like to. Rust to me is a mix of all the great games that I love to play. It's a game I love to play with friends, and one I highly recommend others to pick up. Rust requires no steep learning curve or a super computer. All it takes is a group of friends to embark on a new journey.

After having Mighty No. 9 being a dissappointment and capcom releasing basically only collections of games already released, I missed having a Megaman style game that was original and fun. This MORE than meets that craving I had.
What I liked:
-Platforming is fun and can be fast paced if you can dash properly.
-Although parts of stages may seem familiar in later levels as you get further into a run, the familiar section gets outfitted to make it much more difficult and fresh at the same time.
-Challenge sections help to show mechanics of the game instead of hand holding.
-The unlock system allows you to use the items immediately at the start of the next round so you're not left guessing how they work until RNG lets you.
-Hard mode is customizable and adds an incredible amount of replayability to the game, including options that can make this identical to a megaman game (albeit with one life).
-They were not joking when they said "Crisp precise controls," it is incredibly satisfying platforming and if you make a mistake, you can tell it's not the game's fault for the damage(most of the time).
-If you find the upgrades you've purchased make the game too easy (specifically the OP ones) they can be disabled for more of a challenge.
What I didn't like so much:
-Some of the text in the menu for hard mode challenges (at least at my screen resolution) do not appear fully, and the top and bottom lines of text are cut off so I can't tell what the challenge does completely. This could probably be fixed in later versions.
-Some areas cause guaranteed damage at higher levels which can feel a tad cheap at times.
What I would like to see later:
-More robot masters. It'd be nice seeing some more added to the cast of characters, maybe a second story of sorts (basically advanced mode) where the 8 current are seperated from the 8 new.
-Even more variety to the items, augmentations, enemies and level sections. Some people complain about a lack of variety at this point and I can understand that, however other rogue games, specifically considering the binding of isaac had a limit on room design, enemy design, and more, expanding once wrath of the lamb, rebirth, afterbirth, and afterbirth+ came out. That's when the level design became much larger. I have high hopes for this game to continue growing.
What I hope to add to this review later:
-Multiplayer, I have yet to try out this feature, but it seems very promising and something I've wanted for many megaman games.
I highly reccomend this game and I think it should be a very sought after game for fans of megaman and more.
As a bonus I say check out the soundtrack as well, It's really well done music and I've listened a ton to it. I say the title song, "20XX," is my favorite.

A very fun Mega Man X styled roguelite with a couple of glaring problems.
The most pressing issue in my 10 or so hours of game play is that your basic movement for both characters (which does include a ground dash) leaves a lot to be desired in the later levels. The platforming in level 6 or farther becomes exponentially more difficult if you don't RNG one of the 3 good leg Augs, which because this is a roguelite you have no guarantee to get. It also makes the harder versions of some bosses MUCH harder than they would be if you had decent movement options.
Second, unlocking a lot of the buyable/collectable augs after the first 5 or so runs ends up being a detriment in a lot of scenarios when it just increases the pool of options that you can get from stores/chests for augs. A lot of them are useless depending on existing upgrades and some can be actively bad for you.
On the positive side, the gameplay is immediately familiar to veterans of the Mega Man X series. both the X (Nina) and Zero (Ace) analogues are fun to play and remind you very much do how X and Zero controlled in the early MMX games. The music and sound effects add a lot to the nostalgia of the experience, and fit nicely with the aesthetic of the game.
Overall it's well worth it's price of entry for anyone into Mega Man or old school platforming, and fans of the Mega Man and X series will have a lot of fun here. Definitely recommended.

Since Megaman X is one of my top 10 games of all time and I also love roguelites, I was very excited for 20XX to leave Early Access.  I think this is a fine game and it does feel pretty similar to controlling X complete with charge shots, dash jumping, and wall kicking.  Like Megaman X, the game has 8 boss levels before a couple finale levels.  However, these initial levels will need to be replayed over and over and over in order to have a shot at the finale levels.  There is a very small number of unlockables which makes the roguelite part feel unnecessary and repetitive.  Most upgrades are stat boosts which leads to very similar runs unlike many other roguelites which provide different experiences each time.  On top of that, the early first 6-7 boss levels are pushovers before having a huge difficulty spike that depends heavily on your luck with drops whether it is possible to continue on in the run.  Overall, this isnt a terrible game but with the lack of content it would have been much better as a standard single play game instead of a roguelite which gets too repetitive quickly.  I think most people will have fun for a few hours which might be worth it for a good sale, but beyond that I wouldn't recommend this game.

TLDR: A very short point-and-click puzzle game with a forgettable main character and story. Get it cheap and don’t expect too much and you’ll have a decent time with it.
Long story: Sam Peters was one of the side-characters in Secret Files 2. Here she is again in her own little adventure, starting from where we left her in the previous game. In Secret Files 2 I found her much nicer than the main characters; though mainly because her voice-actress was not completely incompetent. So, is she an interesting enough character to fill out an adventure on her own? Not really. She’s an excellent example of a writer trying to create a “strong female character” without having any clue how. As a result most of her jokes center around her ex-boyfriend’s dangly parts. The story is similarly uninteresting; you are trying to track down a professor in the jungle and when you get there everyone is missing! So, nothing new, but it works.
The puzzle design has the same “charms” and problems as the previous Secret Files games: a ton of items that you are supposed to use, but often a very vague goal that you are trying to accomplish, forcing you to try everything on everything. I found it a bit less annoying in Sam Peters than I did in Secret Files 2; but that’s probably because that was a much longer game which naturally increases the number of times you get annoyed at seemingly unintuitive solutions.
The length of the game (I finished it in about 2h) is a real problem, at least according to other reviews. Personally I think it was the right decision for the game. After all, the main character and the story could probably not support a much longer game. In fact, dragging it out longer would probably have ended up hurting the game more. Still, it means you have to decide what you are willing to pay for such a short adventure game with a rather bland and uninteresting heroine and story. I got it at 75% off at around 2.5 Euro and that was okay for me. Set your expectations low and you may have a good time with Sam Peters.

ONE of the Greatest DmC games hands down.

FYI - I have never played any other DmC game, so my experience is without any background from the previous games.
This game is so beautiful. It's like a walking screenshot. Every single scene, every single demon looks terrific. In the first 20 minutes I made 39 screenshots. When I finished the game the number of screenshots was 529. That's how beautiful and scenic this game is.
Apart from the visuals, great animations, great combat fluidity (holy♥♥♥♥♥♥everything is so smooth!), this game has awesome soundtrack and ambient sounds too. You get a full package of great visual and sound experience.
The story itself is... OK. Nothing unexpected and nothing mindblowing, but decent enough for an action game.
I like how simply you can switch between different weapons during the combat without breaking the immersion.
But this game has some flaws too.
The camera angles is just soooo frustrating sometimes. It forces you to look where it wants not where you want. You just feel the resistance when you want to have a look around while moving the mouse. I accidently jumped of the cliff more than a handful of times because of this.
I really dislike the approach of forced replayability. Sometimes you can't reach something, break something or open a door just because you don't have the tools yet. Sometimes you get those tools only several missions later. And I really hate when games do stuff like this. I just want to play a mission and have the access to everything without worrying about the "locked" content. [I finished the game and I'm really not interested to go back and replay the missions just to open a few doors in order to play some challenges]. It's just not worth your time (unless you really enjoy it...).
One mission is like a copy/paste of Mad Moxxi's Underdome DLC from the first Borderlands. Just too many similarities. But I liked it. it was pretty well done.
Overall, the gameplay feels very segmented: Kill a few waves of monsters, then a few segments of climbing and jumping around. Rinse and repeat. Everytime you see an open area, you can expect a 2-3 demon waves with some strong big♥♥♥♥♥demon at the end. It's always like this. It gets old by the end of the game.
But I enjoyed DmC: Devil May Cry. Main story line is about ~13h long and the dlc is ~2h long.
Oh, as for DLC (Vergil's Downfall) - it's very shallow and soulless, but at least the action is even more for fast paced than in the main game.

This was an amazing game that I'll always enjoy. Took some of the best parts of DMC3's combat and improved it a lot. The new look may not be for everyone, but it grows on you. The style and fun of the game is still there. One of my favorites! The better you get at the game, the more fun it becomes.

Terrible soundtrack, awful writing, and just all around not worth your time. The only redeeming feature of this bland action game is the set pieces in which the color coded fights take place. It's clear ninja theory doesn't really have any idea what makes a game fun and have some very backwards ideas about what constitutes a "cool" character. Between the dumbed down combat which as mentioned before is just matching the colors of your weapons to the colors of the enemies and the constant barrage of edgy "adult" themes this game borderlines as a parody of the genre from which it came. The most offending part is that while the color matching combat is at least serviceable for lower skilled players to mash their way through the game, it limits player's ability to create combos by mixing up what weapons they want to use and when. This creates a very low and shallow experience that seasoned players will come to find themselves bored of quickly and then have to suffer through what amounts to some teenager's fan fiction tier story writing. The highpoint of this game is a few platforming areas that are actually quite decent. In fact the only value this game has comes from the pretty scenery you can explore in between boring waves of recolored enemies. The world around you will shift into a demon land and alter itself in fairly surprising ways. What was once just a roadway will break apart and become an interesting segment where you must use your abilities and equipment to move from place to place. This is a welcome distraction from the terrible combat and story. Speaking of story, here's the worst part of this game by far. No exaggeration, this game has a scene in which one character shoots a pregnant woman through the stomach killing her child and then they shoot her. This is played out as a good thing as said woman and child were demons; however, as this scene takes place neither are in any way portrayed as such. Now these characters are a boss fight in the game, but this scene isn't in anyway connected to this boss fight and it amounts to a distasteful scene of a pregnant woman being shot. The main character even taunts the final boss about it after they ask why it was done. It's this tone deaf writing throughout this game that shows how little ninja theory understand what it takes to make a compelling story/character. I'd say pick this game up only to laugh at as it is basically garbage in electronic form.

It's unintentionally funny. BONUS: Has a Spanish language mod that increases how hilarious it is.
Decent platforming
Excellent set pieces and scenery.
Competent developers from Capcom did try to fix this mess with the definitive edition. So there are some tweaks improving it such as 60fps and more.
CONS:
Terrible soundtrack
Terrible writing

Ori and the Blind Forest is a platformer made my Microsoft and Moon Studios and is an incredible game. What makes this game so great? So many things! The music is beautiful, the visuals are jaw-dropping, the sound design is spot on, and the story is surprisingly touching. The controls are one of the best things about this game. In Ori and the Blind Forest, controlling the character alone is fun, which is a hard thing for alot of games to nail. For every action your character does, it feels absolutely perfect. These incredible controls makes for a surprisingly challenging game in that you'll be having to make some very precise jumps and such. Every death you have, Except for a few cheap deaths which happen every once in a while, is your own fault, which simply gets you to improve yourself as a player and allows for a game that will challenge your skill. The one problem that I do have with the game, aside from the occasional cheap deaths, are moments in the game where the situation becomes dire and intense and you must run for your life. These parts, though fun, will most likely have you dying quite a few times, which can take away some immersion from the game and perhaps might have you going into a bit of a rage. The replayabilaty of this game is also handled very well. There are plenty of hidden areas and extras for you to find, explore, and collect. Ori and the Blind Forest is an absolutely fun game which I highly reccomend to anyone who enjoys platformers. I give this game a 8/10.

1.  It controls very well.  For example, the dash, wall jump, etc. all feel totally natural.  It does all the fundamental things a good platforming game like this should.
2.  The weapons, upgrades, and enemies all vary nicely.

5.  The rogue-like aspects are a lot of fun and give it a lot of replayability.  They don't feel tacked on and give you a lot of choice in how you build your attributes.  This adds a lot to the Mega Man-ish formula, more than I thought it would.

I really wanted to like this game. Megaman X defined my childhood. Still, 20XX falls short. The procedural level element works fine, but comments about each level feeling "samey" ring true. Whenever you sign a contract with The Procedural Devil, it comes with a set of pretty standard drawbacks. If you ever suffered under No Man's Sky, you understand how barren it can feel even when surrounded by abundance. 20XX emulates this feeling when the same enemies appear in each level.
Second, for a roguelike game, I believe 8 bosses is too few to provide the variability and diversity required for sustained replayability. I loved defeating my first boss, walking into the reward room, and seeing 3 fresh Bosses to choose from. "Wow!" I thought. 2 runs later, I was already growing tired of running through the stages to fight bosses that were, unfortunately, well designed aesthetically, but less inspired when it came to difficulty and weapon design. If you ever played the later installments of the X series, you know how laughable some of the powers got and how unrewarding they felt to use. Shooting, literally, a giant blue square, is dumb. This is what the dragon boss in this game rewards you with. Not a flamethrower, not some cool flying dash move....you shoot a giant blue square.
Don't get me wrong--there's a lot of potential for this game with an expansion or sequel. *The bones are good*. The gameplay is smooth, the artwork gorgeous, and the intentions well-made. It may seem like I don't have much positive to say about this game, but the positives are already well-documented in other reviews. There's just too much that slips for me to recommend a purchase.
6.5/10.

It all improves this much over the original formula. And despite the rather unrefined cover art, I think the ingame animation and art is more impressive than Capcom's last attempt at 2d, especially so considering budget.
Anyhow, I do recommend some odd @#%$ at times, but this is definitely a refreshing take on Bluebomber that should be checked out. I will be playing much more of it.

Controlling your monsters in battle can be frustratingly tough because of the lack of any overlap, identical health bars for friendly and enemy, lack of hotkeys/hotgroups, stupid/unpredictable AI behavior, and no strategy interface to coordinate your forces or do anything complex. Upgrading apartments manually takes forever and often is counterintuitive because monsters will demand things they don't actually want or need and frequently when you satisfy requirements and make a really nice apartment the monster you just spent a lot of money pleasing will stop paying rent because now he can't afford it. These kinds of unnatural hurdles are everywhere in this game. Unique nouns in the game generally reference internet games and meme culture, as seems to be the popular tactic of late for flash games where the author doesn't want to do any creative work.
Overall Unholy Heights is not really worth spending money on unless it is VERY cheap and you've got nothing better to do than explore simple flash games. This one is charming at times, with an interesting premise, it just isn't very good.

Indie games are great. They help recapture the magic of gaming that many AAA titles slack on in recent times. With titles like Freedom Planet, Shovel Knight, Undertale, Super Meat Boy, VVVVVV, and tons more delivering quality gameplay and nostalgic overtones whilst providing their own unique universes and stories to tell, all for a usually reasonable price, there’s no limit to the benefits of buying and playing indie titles. However, not every independently made game is golden; in fact, when an indie game is bad, it’s really, really bad. Like, atrocious. Horrid. Abominable. Every negative word in the dictionary. Heartomics is this year’s posterboy for that. It only came out three months ago, but I am pretty sure this is the worst Steam game I’ve ever played, period.
-Graphics-
Thought that trailer was bad? Well, take a look at the actual game!
These graphics look very eerily similar to one of the Game Boy Color Zelda games, as if they were ripped straight from one of them. That said, this game manages to make those graphics look like utter crap. The backgrounds are dreadfully uninspired, and the sprites are not even animated all that properly. The game also loves to spam enemies all over the place, making for only the most visually stimulated kind of graphical vomit.
-Audio-
Thankfully, the trailer’s audio is not at all in the game itself. However, what is in the game is a few unfitting music pieces that don’t seem to mesh well with the messy action onscreen.
-Story-
Story? What story? Heartomics certainly doesn’t tell one! Heck, there isn’t even a title screen! When the game boots up, it throws you straight into a room with an info box that tells you something like “Hey, we’re too lazy to start you out with any weapons, but when you do find them, here are the controls: (Insert weapon controls here)”.
-Gameplay-
Oh, boy oh boy….Let’s start with the controls of this thing. The player can move around with the arrow keys, but it isn’t like diagonal movements exist in this game! Heck, if you press an arrow key different from the direction you’re moving in, you stop dead in your tracks! Are they actually kidding me?! Not only that, but it’s hard to even make out where to even find any weapons to begin with. I eventually came across an area with bombs, but HOLY CRAP their timing for exploding is absolutely horrid. And for no reason whatsoever, I eventually obtained a sword for reasons I don’t know. All I know is I started with it when I tried again one time after I died.
The game is seemingly super strict with survival seeing as how enemies are literally spammed all over what would otherwise be completely empty rooms. And when you die, you don’t just instantly go back to the autosaved checkpoint you came from; you have to press something on your keyboard to actually get to spawn there! And the game doesn’t tell you this!
You know what functions the game also doesn’t tell you? The debug functions that are left right in the game for all two people suckered into playing this to abuse. On my laptop, just pressing F5 grants me the ability to be invincible and run really fast, which is what I assume the developer used to “test” out the “game”, because actually playing this game normally is a death wish. Pressing Fn+F6 granted me loads of rewards that you’d normally obtain from killing certain enemies, including ones that don’t do anything and ones that hurt your health.
And should you even try to play through the game with cheats at hand, you’ll still find yourself with a couple dead ends. As in the game doesn’t seem like it can be beaten at all. After all, I did legitimately take the time to clear out a whole room of baddies and giant ones that I assume are meant to be bosses, but nothing happened.
This game costs money to play.
-Verdict-

It manages to take everything I loved about Mega Man and Mega Man X as a kid and throw it all into a very addictive roguelike that has yet to get stale for me. Even the dash-jumping and wall-jumping feel just as responsive and intuitive as they did in the original X games. The only thing I'd knock this game for is the fact that the randomly-generated nature of the levels leaves them feeling a bit more lifeless than something like the average Mega Man level with a lot of specifically-designed gimmicks, but that's by design. I've never played Mighty No. 9, but I see people saying this is more of a Mega Man revival than that game was, and I can definitely see that. It's surprising that some fans can do Mega Man better than Inafune himself and with a fraction of the Kickstarter budget, but they deserve mad props for doing so.
Mega Man + Rogue-like + Co-op = Good times

tl;dr: Game feels clean and good in single or multiplayer. Appeals to anyone who liked Mega Man X or Roguelikes.
Absolutely loving this game. Powerups are fun and can really change how your run goes. Different Armor Sets feel varied and interesting, evoking thoughts of combining different pieces, but also rewarding you for using a full set for an extra bonus. Dashing and wall climbing feel crisp, clean and fantastic. Feels so great to plow through a level smoothly, when you can make it happen.
Played alot of online co-op in this and it's great. Occasionally de-sync issues between the players, BUT the stage and enemies in relation to you always feels perfect, so the de-sync just looks like a visual bug that doesn't affect gameplay. The difficulty scaling for an additional player feels good, more difficult, but not ridiculously so. Girlfriend has been playing on a keyboard and it's obviously sub optimal, from what I've seen, but the game does strongly recommend you use a controller. Was able to get my old PS3 Dualshock 3 to work with it fantastically with minor fiddling. Highly recommend the game to anyone who liked Mega Man X or likes Roguelikes.

The atmosphere and graphics are excellent. I'm not much of a 2D platformer fan but i really enjoyed this game. I recall at one point in the story you fall into a massive pit and I really felt like i was falling into some kind of trap I admit I was totally scared (lol) it surprised me so bad XD. that's a sign of good atmosphere.
Mechanically the game is amazing, you jump around so elegantly it feels like one of the smoothest games i've ever played (unless lag). It starts simple and as you level up perks the gameplay gets more and more in depth until you're immersed in all the amazing things your character can do. The combat is simple and different, i definitely did not get bored killing monsters and the offense simplicity was important to not detract from the platforming essence of the game. I found this game challenging, and also addicting. when it pushed me, i simply felt like pushing back and trying again. Although some parts I found very difficult (mechanically taxing) and some of the puzzles were confusing (no idea what to do), for most part the game is very open. its yours to explore and you can fight every monster if you like or you can try to just run past everyone, you don't feel pressured to collect every single coin or explore every corner of the map. you can leave things behind and come back to it later if you like. the game is very flexible this way and it helps with coping with any frustrations.
This is the kind of game you want to have the time to sit down and play for awhile. 30 mins - 2 hours is what i would consider optimal. The reason is its hard to simply pick up this game and progress at all in 15 minutes, it takes some effort and I often needed to warm up my hands to make any decent progress to completion. I found time really flied by playing this game, and the shorter 30 minute sessions i recommend often left me wanting more, but i still think that's enough time to explore a new area successfully. The pc version of Grand Theft Auto San Andreas is, well, okay to say the least. It's not a trainwreck like the shoddy pc port of Vice City, but it is not a near masterpiece like the ps2 version of San Andreas. Its middle of the road for me. The reasons behind why I prefer the ps2 version of San Andreas are as follows. The pc version has some game breaking bugs here and there. Its playable, yes, but the bugs and glitches that you have to work around to avoid or fix cripple the experience a bit, not to an insane degree, but they are irritating, like a fly buzzing around your ear, a baby crying or finding a bug in your food. This review is based off of my experience with the game, so the problems you encounter may vary. Such bugs/glitches that I had to put up with/endure were the game crashing every now and then (which makes saving your game alot a nessecity, or face anger/rage), swimming underwater was impossible, certain items would cause the game to crash upon using them, various audio files were missing, some texures were missing, some graphical errors here and there, framerate issues and more that I probably forgot because meh. I would recommend this game because, if you lower your standards and are okay with dealing with the things that I told you about (or other bugs/glitches that you may find yourself) then this game would be okay for you, but understand that the ps2 version is far superior as you would be free of all of the nonsensical bugs/glitches and you could listen to the radio with all of its music stilll within the game. So, to digress, the pc version is tolerable, the ps2 version is near perfect (despite a graphical downgrade). Oh, and I have no idea what the ps3 version is like so I guess its a mystery! :D

After playing around 450 hours. This will be my view of the game.
10/10 amaze.
But seriously. This games has it all. Great story, amazing artstyle, fps gameplay, rpg loot, boss battles, co-op play, insane replay value, vehicle and character customizations, good dlc's. And I could go on and on.
The sheer quality of the quests aint that impressive. Dont get me wrong. They are good but not impressive. You've got your main story and your side quests. Most quests wil obviously you kill quests or pickup quests. But the good thing about those quets is that the quest itself it so well integrated into the story that you dont really pay attention to that its just your regualr old kill quest. Further more. The sheer amount of different weapons makes kill quests way more interessting. Since you have those situations where you pick up a new gun and you are aching to try it out.
Besides the main quests there are alot of fun and interesting side quests. Side quests either have their own story to them. Is related to one of the characters backstory or is just a gimmicky quest. (that should be enough on questing)
The gameplay it just great. It has your simple hack n slack feel wraped up in a first person shooter. Its loot based system and the rpg elements makes the game just so much greater. The constant search for new loot and encoutering new enemies was such a blast! The gameplay it self is simple but so much fun. You've got your 1-4 weapons, a granade and your action skill.
Visuals of the game are something you kinda must like but also will grow on you once the start playing. The combination of the games story and visual art style makes it a great combination. The art style really fits well with the game. I wouldnt want to see it any other way. Thanks to the art style you'll come across some amazing bosses.
DLC's... aah dlcs. I've hated dlc's since they became a thing. But for this game. Woah. I'd buy the dlc's any day of the week. Most of the dlc's gives you alot of play value. Some interessting stories and alot of extra LOOT!! The 4 main dlc's are good. Their stories are well writen and interessting the new characters are fun and the new bosses are just a blast to fight.
Progression in the game is simple. Its has your basic single story line with at the end an option to replay the whole game but on a higher dificulty. Its simple but effective. Ofcourse some will be disapointed that they have the play the same story again and again BUT!! fear not. For increasing the dificulty will also add some new enemies. So thing will stay interessting while you replay the whole story.
In conclusion I'd recommand this game to any one. Are you heavely into FPS or RPG games? No worries this game has it both. Replay value is just amazing. Even after my 450 hours I still learn new things! Game is fun to play solo but even more fun to play co-op! (feel free to message me)

Amazing experience in VR.
I know about ETS2 for a long time already but never got into it. Despite the shortcomings that VR still has, and the fact that ETS2 uses a somewhat outdated game engine, it is an incredible experience in VR. You really *ARE* in the truck. MIND.BLOWN. Turn into a cool radio station and haul cargo in your truck in VR. Awesome experience. You need to try this.
Yet, I hope the devs can improve the VR aspect of this somewhat, eg. performance and the shimmering/low resolution of things in the distance. (I am already playing at 1.4x scale according to cfg, more can't my GTX970 handle ). Cut scenes are also less than optimal for VR. It's experiences like this which make me "shudder" in excitement about gaming in say, 2-4 years, when VR gets even better. THIS is so real I caught myself wanting to hold out my arm from the truck window to "feel the breeze". (Or when you play a flight sim like P3D and you wouldn't be surprised if the small door in the back opens and a flight attend comes in, serving you coffee. Yes it feels THAT real. No comparison to playing on a screen, folks!).  If you want "real", play this in VR!!

An offshoot in the Secret Files series with a minor character from part two, Puritas Cordis, getting her own little adventure in the jungles of Africa. While being very short compared to the rest of the games in the series, this one is actually the first one that's on par with the original - that is, perfectly acceptable, albeit not especially great adventure on a budget.
Sam Peters is a better protagonist than Nina Kalenkov, even though she does still blurt out wildly inappropriate stuff every once in a while and definitely has a bit of a snooty attitude. Anyhow, the story is more in line with Animation Arts' best effort, Lost Horizon: A traditional Indiana Jones -style romp that deals with uncovering existing mysteries of the world instead of inventing new ones or trying to provide a modern angle on things.
The graphics have improved a bit, the voice acting is perfectly serviceable and the puzzle design is actually quite nice. I never got desperately stuck, so I guess this is one of the easier entries in the series. You can definitely see the budget trappings of the game though - Almost no other characters besides Sam, exposition done mostly with static comic book -style panels and text, pretty lukewarm ending etc. etc. Still, I'd say this is not a waste considering the price, and will aggravate the player much less than some of the other Secret Files entries.

Absolutely fantastic.
This is Mega Man X meets Rogue Legacy. Mega Man style powers up, controls, and weapons. But Rogue Legacy randomness and getting some permanent upgrades between runs.
The only thing that isn't randomly generated is the power up that a boss drops, that's fixed. Outside of that it's allllll random. Level order? Random. Item drops? Random. Stats upgrades? Random. Level layout? Random.
Now, it isn't a strict random, it's more that the level layout has a few major sections that select from a group. So you will see the same layouts appear many many times. What keeps it fresh is the enemy and hazards within that layout.
Sure I'll have seen these 5 platforms before, but I didn't see them dipping down into a laser beam, with vertical lazers between each of them making my jumps a lot harder.
Oh look. Different level, those same 5 platforms. But they vanish this time, and I have fireballs blasting up where I need to jump.
It would be nice for there to be more variety in the fixed platform layouts, but that in no way detracts from an amazing game.
I use an XBox 360 controller for windows, I don't know how I would play this game without one. Or at least without another controller. I would not advise anyone to try this game just with the keyboard.
EDIT:
An addition to the review. Higher difficulties alter level layouts, adding a LOT more complexity and making it a lot harder to avoid damage. So you may not even recognise the similar layouts due to the addition of so many traps. So my biggest complaint in wanting more variety is already answered in what the higher difficulties provide.
However, some of the boss powers are able to manipulate the environment, able to prevent some of the 'traps' from working. I won't say what or how to not spoil it. But it really adds more strategy to what powers to take from what bosses.
I've also been really enjoying running the daily challenge. Everyone gets everything unlocked, and gets the exact same seeded level layouts, then it's a race to see who can get the most points and finish the fastest!
This is the true Megaman X reimagining,buy it NOW! We need more games like this.
I highly recommend this game and I hope the devs keep adding new boss and enemies.  I have a feeling this game could become the next Binding of Isaac if it had a bit more content.

Also, there are over 100 of them, so, if you want to 100% this game, you're gonna be putting in some time. It's a nice mix of Mega Man X with a rogue-lite. Gorgeous visuals and versatile movement mechanics help
stand out from the pack, but otherwise, it's standard Metroidvania fare.  "Dungeons" and an NPC companion give it a dash of Zelda, and the periodic escape sequences are reminiscent of Rayman Origins/Legends.
Secrets are dense and rewarding, at least until lategame, but (with one exception in the Definitive Edition) don't expect to uncover whole secret areas.  At times, the game can feel a bit linear for a Metroidvania, possibly so it can accommodate story elements (which are decent).  Giving the player a helpful NPC companion prevents the feelings of isolation and disorientation common in the genre, which is fine, but if it decides to go that route, it should also populate its world with more NPCs to engage with.
The combat is nothing spectacular, since aiming is automatic, but the game understands this and makes up for it with heavy platforming.  Still, there's a conspicuous lack of large bosses to fight, which seems like a strange design decision.
felt short with only
dungeons (with Mount Horu having the best design, in my opinion), but it also seems like it'd be a fun game to speedrun because there is a lot of freedom of movement.
The Metroidvania genre has plateaued a bit since
defined it all the way back in 1994.
adds a couple new (and fun) movement mechanics, but it lacks an experimental hook.  I would recommend
over this game, even though
is less technically proficient.

I would recommend this game because, if you lower your standards and are okay with dealing with the things that I told you about (or other bugs/glitches that you may find yourself) then this game would be okay for you, but understand that the ps2 version is far superior as you would be free of all of the nonsensical bugs/glitches and you could listen to the radio with all of its music stilll within the game. One thing to know about this game: It's adorable. It's not addicting, but it is a pretty good game to waste some time on, or just to try something new. It has its troll moments, and I was grinning at some of the dialogue the monsters made. You're the devil in this game. You don't take over the world or be evil, you simply give monsters a place to live, make sure they're satisfied to become stronger, watch them live their lives, and fight guilds off.
Butttt, getting into the deep side of this game.. You have to choose your tennants wisely. Depending on their job, they'll be able to pay the rent, more or less. If they're for example a window washer, obviously they'll be very poor and probably won't even be able to pay off 14g's worth of rent. You get rent every day, which lasts for about 30 seconds if you have x3 speed.
What's cute about it is that not only the artstyle is cute and cuddly but the literal whole story. I mean, the game has unholy in it, and you're playing as the devil. But it's really not that at all, it's just like a hotel tycoon game with monster characters. Not to mention you get to see your tennants running back home in the rain scared, poor tennants that aren't able to pay rent will usually have a nervous or timid status (but is still able to fight), and little baby skeletons and chicklings. <:
It's a bit strategic as well. Waiting to get a good monster that has a good job and has high damage in health is kind of the learning part to the game. You get to learn which jobs pay more unless of course you're an actual person and actually know how much an amateur boxer and/or an unpopular comic creator gets paid.  Different monsters have different pleasures too, some guys like the room hot, some like it cold. Some don't care if it's clean, some really mind. Cheap furniture will suffice for beginning monsters but as you progress they're going to request for more expensive items - especially the demons. But the demons are pretty damn helpful in battle.
Speaking of battle, you do have to wait a while to start new quests, just so your monsters can regen health get a +1 on their attack, but I enjoy this kind of stuff.
Excuse my sleep deprived mind as I am only using %8 of my brain at the moment, but seriously, it's a dollar, or at least it is in the holiday sale, I wouldn't recommend buying it for the full $4. It should be worth $2 max.

Unholy Heights is a game to buy at a nice low price-point.
While many critics have labeled it a "tower defense" game, it really isn't. Unholy Heights is a classic monster-breeding game. You invite in monsters, improve their stats, have generations of children, and occasionally fight off heroes who want to rob you of your hard earned rent monies.
If you don't enjoy spending hours on end trying to coax monsters into breeding with one another, you should probably avoid this one. It can be won without monster breeding, but it's really hard.
The game deliberately doesn't tell you a lot of the secrets you'll want to know to breed up great monsters. In that respect, it follows in the footsteps of Monster Rancher, Viva Pinata, and other games of the sort that left you scrambling for a comprehensive Guide. This has been folks' biggest complaint about the title, which seems silly as a lot of the stuff most reviewers complain about is actually documented in the game (It tells you right up front in the Bestiary, for example, that Abyssals and Chimerae hate one another. Or that Demons are only happy when lots of residents are dying all the time).
It's cute, cheap, and hours of fun. If you're a fan of the genre, buy this when it's under $5. It's a steal.

This is my first time buying an early access game - and so far, I'm delighted. I've been sucked into the survival/crafting/resource management genres for a while now, and after seeing a brief bit of gameplay for this on youtube, I wanted to give a try myself.
As someone that completely adores pixel graphics as well as cell shading, I find this low poly game just freaking adorable. I play on a 40" television, and it holds up quite well even at that size (and on a low end tv). My PC isn't a beast by any stretch of the imagination, but it still runs this quite smoothly (excluding about 5 seconds when flying down to the surface at the start of the game).
I've only been playing for a little over an hour, so I can't say how it holds up for long-term play, but so far, I can see that it won't be a game that I'll play on a daily basis. Picking it up once or twice a week would be nice, as it is a very calming game.. despite being somewhat eerie. I also love finding games that I can play with my young nephews - games that won't bore me to tears.
All in all, I say that if you enjoy the crafting genre, this may be worth a small $20 investment, especially if they continue to expand. The bugs I've run into so far have been mostly minor, and really, it's early access, so I expected my game to break now and then. I report it and move on - and hope that all the fiddliness in early access will make it a low bug game on release.

Pros:

I remember being pretty upset when this game came out, I hated the design choices, the dumbing down of the game, and all the other changes. I finally did pick up the game for $7.50, and I have to say, it's really good. I'll break everything down:
The gameplay: Despite dumbed down, the gameplay is very fun. Everything feels really polished and smooth, and still allows you to do really cool looking combos, but it is a lot easier and feels less rewarding.  This really isn't that much of a deal, as it is nice to just sit back, and enjoy a game casually. The boss fights are fantastic, each feel really creative and intense, but lack depth, and are pretty easy.  This game also features a little bit of 3D platforming, while it is very simple and does a lot of hand holding, it still looks pretty cool, and isn't terrible. The level design is really good, but it gets al little annoying towards the end, but some levels just are pure magic in this game, fitting the syle of the game, and accommodating for fighting excellently The gameplay is definitely really good though, everything feels great, despite being a lot simpler.
The graphics/aesthetic: The game has a very flashy, bright, and hyperactive style to it, kind of like it was designed by someone with ADD. Don't view that as a bad thing, because the art style works really well for this type of game. The way the environments contort and change, is incredible, it's easily the best part about the game visually, it's some really impressive stuff. The one thing I was on the fence about, was the design of Dante. His design isn't super great, there's just something off about his appearance in the game, but this can be easily changed by getting the costume pack and using the classic Dante skin, it makes him look much better.
The writing: This is definitely the weakest point of any hack and slash game, but I have to say, it's not bad in this. The story is okay, it works, and I was intrigued. The one liners are okay, they're certainly not as intelligent, but I liked them. The dialogue is a little weak though, some exchanges between characters feel awkward and forced. It's okay most of the time, but sometimes it can get pretty bad.
The music: While all the previous games did a more instrumental type of metal, DMC: Devil May Cry, went more a much more electronic metal. It's great, but it fits the style of the game, and does its job. I didn't mind it, but it can feel a little overbearing at times, and tries a little to hard to be edgy.
DMC: Devil May Cry may have a dumb title, and a few issues, but if you're looking to have some classic hack and slash action, and not much of a challenge, I'd definitely recommend this game. It's really good, and while I don't agree with some design choices, I had a fantastic time playing this game, it's just so good.

Megaman being one of my favorite series has given me an itch for some time I have yet to scratch, but 20XX has hit that mark and left me wanting more. At first I thought I was going to play this game and be disappointed after a little while, but before I knew it 4 hours had passed and I had not yet beaten it. Another 5 hours later I managed to finally beat the game, and I was ready to quit, but I realized I still had many other things in game to unlock to power me up more. I am 11 hours into this game and I have to admit it is far more addictive than what I thought it would be originally.
Pros:
Random level patterns smushed together for interesting layouts
Enemies slowly gain strength as you progress
Items are random and MANY combinations work well together (I almost never collect powers, always grab me nuts for more items)
Bosses and enemies are tiered pretty fairly and never seem to overpower you
Use of a controller makes the game a cakewalk (though you should remap your keyboard and gamepad, the default button layout sucks horribly)
Music is very reminiscent of the SNES Megaman games I miss
Online play is pretty dope, though only using emojis to communicate is pretty annoying
11 hours in and I am still sure there is a ton of stuff to unlock
Cons:
Sometimes trap timing is nearly impossible to get through without a lot of speed or jumping/flying past everything
Some enemy attacks glitch through walls making it hard to dodge when you are cornered
Sometimes you wont find a health station for 3-4 levels
Most of the powers are useless, seriously, use the reflect shield or dragons power, the others are too crummy in comparision
Ace has terrible attacks, yet everyone wants to use him online
No quick save for resuming later
Some platform glitching has killed me numerous times dropping through the base of them
Summary:
I don't normally leave reviews, but this is something I think anyone who likes to test their skill will enjoy, it's great for long or short play sessions. Now if you'll excuse me, I think I am going to put another 11 hours in this game.

4 hours in, haven't even broken level 4. Some of the most enjoyment i've had for a while, from a seemingly innocuous game. The difficulty settings having gotten my friend who is bad at games to play are great if you're not-so-great at games but still want to enjoy the experience - Easy seems to be a good experience that isn't so easy it's insulting.
Highly recommend to any fan of Megaman X, at any skill level. You will at the very least get your money's worth.
An edit after a bit more playtime: the game is far more varied than I originally thought. If you feel like you're bashing your head againt the wall too much and everything gets samey, don't worry - the levels do get more varied as you get further.

ive spent a fair amount of time on 20XX completing the game on normal. i purchased the game on sale for $12 and felt like i got my moneys worth. i enjoyed the graphics, gameplay, music, the FEEL of the game. it feels great. i question some design choices. runs can be highly RNG based on what set pieces you found and what items were available for purchase. you can have one run fully decked out dealing insane amounts of damage and having utility, mobility, and survivability. you can also have a run where 75% through you come to terms with the fact you wont be completing a buster build so you have to start buying points for powers or vice versa. that can be really frustrating. the only other thing i will really criticize is the story. there isnt much of one. i got into megaman when the X series came out and story was a big deal to me. part of what kept me from trying out mighty no. 9 was that it looked really childish.

Unholy Heights is a cute little management sim, coupled with defending your building from attackers.
Keeping residents happy is simple enough, give them what they want and don't charge them too much for the room. Getting the residents to actually pay you is tougher, you have to balance not doing quests to give them time for work with doing quests for the big rewards. Sometimes even that won't lead them to pay you as particular monsters are just bad with money.
Residents find partners and can have babies with increased stats, making balancing the items in the room a bit more challenging, but still simple enough.
The combat is simple too, enemies come, you knock on the doors to call residents to fight. But they can't pass each other in the halls, so the order and timing of the door knocks is important.
A good time waster that will eat away the day.

Batman: Arkham Origins is the 3rd entry in the Batman franchise, a prequel to Asylum. Notably, Origins was not developed by the original developers Rocksteady, instead it was made by WB Games Montréal. And oh boy, does it show. Set 5 years before Asylum, Origins portrays a young Batman who has yet to become the superhero vigilante. The thugs and criminals are afraid of him, the police even more so. On Christmas Eve, a hit is put on the Dark Knight by Black Mask. $50 million for the head of Batman, with 8 super-villains competing with each other for the bounty. It could have been neat story, but Origins falls apart in its execution and game-play.
Batman has not met any major villains, yet in one night, goes up against the Joker, Bane, the Riddler, Penguin, Black Mask, Killer Croc, and the Riddler. Not to mention the other B-D list villains such as Electrocutioner, Copperhead, Shiva, Mad Hatter, Deathstroke, Firefly and Deadshot. It’s unbelievable that Batman encountered every one of them for the first time in the same night, much less beat them all.
While this title in the Arkham series doesn't adhere to the visual standards set by Asylum and City, it is still an enjoyable edition to the franchise.
Pros:
- Interesting Story
- Excellent voice acting
- Has replay-ability value
- Lots to do, map is filled with network relays, data packs, informants and side missions
- Boss battles are some of the best in the series
- Added the Bat-cave (Finally!)
- Alfred
Cons:
- Half of the map was made with assets reused from Arkham City and is fairly bland
- Not even close to as detailed as the previous games
- Far too many bugs
- Combat is decent but has a fair amount of kinks
- Fails to innovate and set itself apart Arkham City
- multi-player part is shut-down since 4th of December 2016
- cheesy batman one-liners
Rating: 8/10

Batman. Arkham Origins is basically more of the same from what has been seen from previous Arkham titles, continuing with Arkham Knight which I have not played yet.
It is the same combat system, same story really, same get-xp-for-your-efforts-level up-and-get-better-equipment, same level structure, same kinda quests, just same same same. And that does not make a bad a game by any means.
I believe that was some reviewer once that said that this game is rather grey, and I have to agree. There are not a lot of colours in this game. It is rather bland, but I do not really care.
However, it does not revolutionize anything either. It is a game predicated on an already tested and proven formula given the previous Batman titles, so for some it's a no-brainer to pick this game up, since it cannot dissapoint. For others it can be since as just another cash-grab by devs to cash in a franchise that, remarkably enough has not been tainted and wrecked considering how old Batman is, both as a character and a universe.
The question one might ask is, does game have to break ground? Or should it? And that is a question I have been asking since having seen the aftermath of Arhkam Knight's rather painful, bloody and trouble birth. I do really know. For me it does not have to. I take it for it is, in my opinion, a great game. Simply put!
The story takes place before the story in Arkham Asylum - pre-Joker, pre-Poison Ivy even though the first mentioned makes his grand appearence in the game. We are introduced to the character the Joker as opposed to the previous titles that presumed you had prior knowledge of said person.
Some might be disapointed in the fact that Mark Hamill is not the voice of the Joker, nor is the original voice actor from the previous games present as the voice of "Bats", but I could care less. As far as I am concerned I could not tell the difference. All voice actors do a wonderful job.
I would call the story a-fill-out-the-blanks-kinda story even though you do not necessarily need to know all that happened prior to the narrative in Arhkam Origins. Even still, you do get emerged into it. There is a lot of atmosphere in game.
You play a younger, more angry, more bat(man)-out-of-hell*pun fun in the sun* Batman / Bruce Wayne who, at that point cares little for police, and even less for criminals. Brucie-boy seems more angry and bitter at everything, yet more juvenile and immature than preivous titles. Batman is more about exacting a more violent kind of vigilantism in my opinion.
The main story will have you playing for about 15-20 hours I'd say, and that is excluding the DLC and testing trials.
Anyway, enough BS. Get this game if you liked the previous titles. Again, more of the same, though that should not put you off. Get it while it is on sale with all the DLC. You will not be disapointed.

20XX is one of the best Mega Man experiences out there, and is currently my favorite game of all time. While this game is definitely worth the $15 price, I've seen negative reviews from players who did not read the description, or simply don't know what a roguelite entails. Maybe it's silly to hope that they'll read the reviews by chance, but it's worth a shot.
20XX has permadeath, which means you have to beat all 8 "robot masters" and the two Sigma-esque stages with their respective bosses all in one go. This will be a lot trickier than normal, since the levels are generated using hand designed segments, so memorizing the levels isn't an option. To compensate for this, there's a variety of powerups that you can receive along the way which will make the trip easier, and they are
more powerful than you would fine in an X game. You'll be receiving large boosts to your damage, speed, jump heigh, health, and max energy. There are also more unique powerups, like shooting through walls, different busters/blades, a front facing dash shield, etc. In addition, pits and spikes do not instakill you, so don't worry about that.
Progression works a bit differently as well, since you're intended to die/win and repeat the experience over and over again. During a run through the levels, you'll occasionally find glowing enemies which are a lot tankier than their normal variants. When you kill these enemies, you gain soul chips, which allow you to unlock power ups which will show up in future runs. If you have unlocked all the power ups, you can still use soul chips to bring 3 of them with you into a run, prevent power ups from showing up at all that run, or buy tokens to hopefully get more power ups from slot machines sometimes found at the end of a level.
Ace, the not-Zero, plays a little bit differently when you're using his default saber. Instead of the having a variety of slashes like air slash, rolling slash, dash slash, etc, you simply have access to the triple slash combo
. You can triple slash when standing still, while dashing, while jumping, while wallclimbing, you can use it absolutely anywhere. If you want the rolling air slash (understandable), you can find it as an alternative weapon called the Spinning Glaive. Both the not-X and not-Zero character have alternate weapons to find, so try them all out and see which fits you best.
The movement in 20XX is very similar to Mega Man ZX. You can dash and turn around while still maintaining the dash speed, and you go straight up when you walljump instead of slightly off the wall (though the straight walljump was a glitch in ZX). In addition, you can hold the dash button to dash jump or dash walljump without actually performing a dash, like in X4 onwards. Other than that, it's not too different from a standard X game until you start getting the power ups that increasing your speed, increasing your jump height, or give you additional abilities like air dash and double jump.
Another big change to the formula would be the co-op. If you're playing local co-op, the camera will pan out to show both of you, and if you're playing online co-op, you get your own separate screens. Both characters have their own iframes against bosses, so both players can wail on a boss at the same time without getting in the way of each other. Finally, you have an emote wheel and a teleport feature which you can use by not selecting an emote for roughly 3 seconds
Finally, you have the boss powers. When you beat a boss, you have the option to pick between its power, some money (usable at shops), or a power up. You have access to all boss powers you've picked up in the pause menu, but you can bind three of them to buttons, so unless you have the power cycling option on, you no longer have to deal with clumsily flipping through your powers. All powers share the same energy meter, but they also only consume one energy per use.

If you tell people about a game where you play as satan, they’ll probably think of torturing innocent souls, razing cities, fighting against god… You know, wreaking havoc on an untold scale. That could work, but it probably wouldn’t be nearly as fun as what Unholy Heights’ developers thought of.
"The Devil’s spent his savings on a place in the projects!" is the line that opens the game. Satan now owns an apartment building, and has to bring monsters in as tenants to not only get some cash, but also to protect the place from foolish adventurers looking to slay him. Priorities, see,
all those folks are dead, and we’ve some money in the bank, then we’ll talk about that havoc, and about world domination.
You have a side view of the building. Whenever you’re attacked, the adventurer party will climb floor by floor, attempting to reach The Devil’s room, and you have to call on his tenants to prevent that from happening. When you're not under attack, you’ll need to recruit more tenants and keep them happy, so they’ll fight better and pay more rent. Of course, you aren’t above evicting them if they fail at either of those things.
It’s very engaging, not only because of the gameplay, but the cute cartoon-ish presentation keeps you attached to each monster as they form their families and advance in their careers. It’s hard not to like them, or not feel slightly saddened when they die or leave. But, back to mechanics, the engagement also owes a lot to the surprising amount of depth to the game.
Higher tier monsters have to be unlocked, and each has its own demands for that to happen, demands which aren’t always simple to meet. As you unlock those monsters, you’ll also need to mind the room allocation for battle: some monsters can tank more hits while others work better shooting from afar. To say nothing of the stat growth mechanics.
Still, you can learn most of it in a few hours, without worry. It is truly a gem of an indie game, bringing together management, tower defense and real-time strategy, and still remaining quite accessible. You will need to read guides if you go for 100% completion, but whether or not you decide to, Unholy Heights still offers incredible value for its low asking price of four dollars.

A really interesting game that combines tower defense elements with apartment management.   You play as the Devil who invests in an apartment complex with your tenants being monsters of various types, grouped into seven different races.  Each type of monster is acquired differently and brings different abilities into the fold.  These abilities and the different roles are shared by monsters from different races.  Want a monster with lifesteal but not to kill so many tenants to get the Vampire?  Don't worry, zombies can steal life too!  Need a tank?  You can find one in almost every race!
The game does feel limited and at some point it got to feel repetitive.  The quests are almost all the same except in what adventurers attack you.  When you're not doing quests then most of your time is spend managing the apartment complex which consist of either buying the right furniture and amenities to please your tenants or doing what little you can to influence who lives where (moving people in is easy compared to trying to get one tenant to move in with another tenant).  However, if you like management games like I do, then this game is worth picking up, especially if it's on sale!
