I really wish I could give this game a 'so-so' instead of a solid Thumbs up or down.
The main reason for this is that some people could simply appreciate this game for it's outstanding visuals/audio. I can appreciate this.
However, that doesn't quite cut it for me.
I found this game's lacklustre storyline was overshadowed by the rather annoying difficulty spikes.
Even on 'Normal' mode.
This was exacerbated by the fact that the controls, and Ori, tend to do some annoying things at times.
Ori will often cling to objects in chase-scenes, or, when attempting to perch ontop of thin platforms, Ori will vault over them. This leaves you in this constant state of trying to jump back and forward as Ori keeps latching on to the sides/vaulting around everywhere you don't want. This, yet again, can often lead to death.
Accidentally press even a
down on your stick as you jump somewhere? Expect to launch yourself into
as Ori power stomps to her doom.
This may sound like a minor gripe, but it happens enough, and causes enough deaths, to leave a bitter taste in your mouth.
I detest this trial-and-error garbage in games.
Ori often has scenes where they play out like chase-scenes wherein you must run and avoid various obstacles as something chases you. The issue here is, you are almost
to die over and over each little inch forward you take as you play out the scene.
This doesn't become a challenge. It becomes tedious.
More on this point; there are often traps that you will run into without warning.
Now, you may think "isn't that the purpose of a trap?".
Well, it is a game. You should be rewarded for skill and observation. Not punished without warning or even a chance to react.
Some of these traps lay camouflaged by the background/foreground so much that you can barely tell if the 'trap' is a part of the game.
The same goes for some of the simple 'spike' traps. You can barely tell (at times) which is the background, and which will hurt you.
To further this point (one more time), there are often a lot of visual effects going on with enemies shooting exploding projectiles, as you shoot, as they also explode....as you are also expected to somehow spot the 'other' incoming projectile to dodge (this one being fired from somewhere off screen).
It's too much. There are often times you simply cannot avoid getting hurt.
One saving grace here is that you can save rather frequently. Though there are areas that will not permit this. Sometimes they seem to come from nowhere and leave you backtracking an annoying puzzle-room you forgot to save after.
Look, this game wasn't all bad. There were some nice moments. Though, as you will see in many other reviews, these tend to favour the art and visuals.
I had high hopes for this game, and I understand that down-voting a game rated as 'Overwhelmingly Positive' is not going to attract the kind of thoughtful attention one would hope for.
But I have to give a fair set of balance to these scales. I'm not going to jump on the bandwagon of praising a game solely due to teary-eyed intros, or cutesy characters with nice visuals/music.
By the first 2 hours into the game, it became less about "wow this game is fantastic", and more about "I just want to beat this game so I can put it back on the shelf.."
Once more; while I have the game as a Thumbs-down, my honest recommendation is that it's a so-so game.
Perhaps if I went into the game knowing these things beforehand, I would have known better what to expect, and not have had my original expectations shattered....(which may have led to a Positive review).
Take that under consideration if you are on the fence.

EDIT: After having a second account banned for cheating when I was not cheating, one of which was one I had spent money on, I'm going to have to say that since I have now lost a total ~550 hours of time spent on this game, it was an overall negative experience. Such a shame, it could be so fun if there was more community interaction and the customer support at least TRIED to discuss.
This game is great. Best customization I've ever seen in a game. You can have leggings with a hamburger pattern, or a Strawberry Fish tramp stamp.
Also, it's just about all free, premium just lets you use more at once.
The only beef I really have with the customization is the fact that the minimum boob size isn't really all that small.
The driving physics can be really wonky, but really funny. For example, flipping when you clip the ~2 inch elevated curb, or trying to go in circles and clipping a wall, resulting in your car lying on its side.
Your character and Weapons can all have mod slots, which usually have upsides and downsides, so you don't just have a sniper LMG with no downsides.
The combat is pretty fun. Basically you run around like a maniac while holding/spamming LMB and trying to keep your crosshair on the other guy. It's more fun than it sounds, trust me. I also notice almost no latency issues such as you being shot just after going behind cover.
Now, something important to note is that this game WILL make you angry. To properly enjoy it, you have to be able to deal with getting stomped. And stomped again. And again. But after the dust and tears clear, you'll stand up, and find that after hours upon hours of being pounded into the ground, you're now a gold, and beating most of your peers and even a fair few players who outrank you. The stomping doesn't go away forever, and comes back from time to time, and usually when this happens, I get quite worked up, but I just play some other game for a while. It probably helps that I have a bit of a masochistic side to me, but I ALWAYS find myself coming back. It might be a couple hours, it might be a day, it might be a week, once it was even months. I was just playing other games, mostly Planetside 2 and Dota 2, I had decided that G1 was nothing but a money grubbing game killing company that barely moved the development along at all.
Then one day I decided, "Hey, maybe I'll check out the APB forums. It's not like I have anything better to do." I don't really have a habit of browsing the forums, but I found a thread that compiled codes for free items and premium. Seeing the headphones code, I realized the immense customization this game had, and thought about how cool it would be to make myself look like Sweet Autumn in-game. Eh, why not? It's not like I'm losing anything by playing a couple rounds. I had put on three days of free premium off the codes thread, and I realized that everything just felt a lot better. In my time away from APB, thanks to Planetside and Dota, my aim and reaction time had greatly improved, and I won A LOT of matches. And on top of that, I was earning a lot more money thanks to the premium. A few days later I realized that between the thread and a couple of events that gave small amounts of G1C, I had amassed enough G1C to buy a Joker Mystery Box. I figured there was nothing else I'd spend the tiny sum of G1C on, so I tried my luck, hoping I'd get crazy luck and get a legendary weapon. I didn't, but I did get 30 days of premium, which was pretty cool.
I sat back and realized, "Hey, I'm actually having a lot of fun now, especially with all the improved customization thanks to all this free premium." Since I loved the carbine weapon type so much, I bought the permanent version (Which had like three sales on it at the time) off of the Armas Marketplace.
Then, there was a guy standing near a spawn point at a mailbox. He turned around and shot me. I fired one shot back. He invited me to his group. I figured "Why not?" Long story short I now have a cool new friend because he shot me.
You know, for a low-down, money grubbing, game-killing company, G1 does a pretty good job.

Believe it or not, HITMAN™/Hitman 2016 is one of the best games you can get right now on Steam. This was meant to be a real return to form for the series, following the release of the disappointing Hitman: Absolution in 2012, so fans of the series were understandably concerned prior to the game's release last year.
But not only does HITMAN™/Hitman 6 manage to live up to expectations and meet the standards set by the first four Hitman games; it actually overcomes them and raises the bar to a whole new level. The in-game areas are bigger, more complex and more open than ever before in the series. And there's quite a few of them, along with a huge number of challenges, escalations, additional missions and community contracts. There's a ton of replay value on offer here.
The gameplay is excellent, and offers a much better version of the classic stealth-action core of the Hitman experience. It patches up almost all of the issues Absolution introduced and introduces some new elements, as well. In terms of production value, you're definitely getting your money's worth. HITMAN™/Hitman The Series really feels like a AAA title, with solid graphics, great sound design and terrific music. The levels are superbly and intricately designed, and the variety of locales on offer here really rivals Blood Money.
The biggest problem in HITMAN™/Episodic Hitman is the always-online system, and the Elusive Targets. I don't think these ideas are an appropiate fit for the series, which has always been about a great offering of replayable singleplayer content. Shoehorning time-limited missions into the formula doesn't mesh well with that. After completing them, you're not even given an option to replay them, which is just absurd IMO. Hopefully IOI will rework the system for Season 2, because right now it's a huge black mark on what is otherwise a terrific must-buy.

Spec Ops: The Line, or "yet another cover based third person military shooter..." was my first thought when looking at it in 2012 when it was released.
Then I read more and more about the story, the moral choices and after a couple of months I couldn't resist purchasing it on a sale. I remember starting to play it but never really giving it a chance at first so I stopped playing. Having read more about what a great game it was I gave it another chance, and that was the right decision.
During six days I played through the game twice, the second time was just to be able to see where the choices I hadn't made in the first run would lead me (and to give FUBAR difficulty a try).
The gameplay itself is fairly basic, move between areas filled with cover where waves of enemies will come at you from different spawns and you'll have to fight your way through. That was what I didn't really like about the game at first, but the big thing is the story and how it is presented as you play through the game.
Even today when someone asks for a good single player game, Spec Ops: The Line is the first I ask if they've already played. Some have complained that it's old but that doesn't take away from the fact that it is an great experience.
Just make sure to play through it once without using any guides that will give away details. If you want to unlock all the achievements, just do that during the second playthrough (that is required anyway since you have to beat the game once on the hardest difficulty to unlock FUBAR).

Don't let my playtime fool you as I have played this game a lot more in offline mode...which unfortunately messed my achievement progress up.
That's kinda the feeling you get as you stomp around in this game trying to figure out what to do. It reminds me a lot of Simon's Quest and other super cryptic games. The difference is this game brings a certain charm that makes you want to try to solve the mystery of what the hell is going on. Why did you click on this game? Why are you considering buying it? Why are you reading my review? Because this game's uniqueness is enough to make you want to dive in. It happened to me one college debate trip as me and my best friend were strolling the steam store to kill time. "Da fuq is that?" I asked...and thus....an adventure was born.
To detail out what charm I'm refering to, I'll create a list of the things this game does well in the unique department.
These are the main race of the game. You play as one and are surrounded by tons of them. I think the wum looks like a mound of bird poop, my friend who discovered this with me called them potato balls and my girlfriend calls them marshmellows. What exactly is he? He is....a wum....like the game doesn't compare them to anything we know but rather invents something new. It'd be like trying to describe a human to an alien who comes from a world where humans are not present. Like imagine if an alien race didn't sit in chairs, they didnt have a need to sit. Trying to explain why a human sits might be rather difficult. Wums are...beings that kinda just...mill about doing stuff....while shooting gum out of a gun at enemies...yeah it's kinda hard to explain these characters.
I'm not ganna lie, I'm not a big story person. I do not like games that have a huge focus on story, where you end up watching/reading more than actually playing. However, there is some games that have amazing lore that is told in ways that keep me captivated. A few examples is Doom 3 with the use of PDA Audio Logs to immerse the player in the world of the UAC, Dark Souls with mysterious characters and item descriptions that give hints to what's happening, or lastly Bethesda games that rewards exploration with explainations of what is happening. Wuppo follows this scheme by borrowing from all of these elements. You explore, you find film strips which are like Doom 3's audio logs, meet strange unqiue potato balls and discover that the lore is as deep as the pacific ocean. The developers invented an entire ecosystem, civilization and history.
9 times out of 10 I turn off game music. It takes a lot for me to leave the music on, the soundtrack has to be something magnificent for me to leave it on. Doom 1993, Starbound, Deus Ex: Human Revolution, Saints Row, Grand Theft Auto are examples of games where I leave the music on. Wuppo's soundtrack is expansive, it has a lot of tracks, and they are all really catchy. I end up singing some of the songs that get stuck in my head. Just in case you thought there was lyrics to these songs, by singing I mean going "boop boop booooooooooo looooo dooo choooo". The music reminds me of retro titles on Nintendo or Sega consoles.
If I'm going to mention the charms, I better point out the so-so elements to the game.
I dunno, platformers are so...bleh for me. Sonic the Hedgehog 2 is one of my favorite games of all time but almost purely for nostalgic reasons. This is kinda how platformers are for me as a 21 year old, memories of a time when I used to like platformers. In Wuppo you do some hardcore parkour to get to places you need to go. Considering that some areas have no parallax and the screen just changes, it makes it hard to get from point A to point B. In Sonic you run left to right and the screen scrolls, this is parallax. In Fallout 3/NV/4 when you enter a door it has a temporary load screen then you pop out on the other side, this is screen change. Now pretend the screen change is instant without a load time, I am having a hard time coming up with an example in another game, because the screen doesn't scroll it leaves you disoriented and wondering where you are on said screen. This is Wuppo in some areas. Sometimes there is parallax, sometimes there isn't. Last part of the gameplay is combat. You shoot at gun at enemies, it does a certain amount of damage, you got to evade the enemies to survive and you can use health items to keep yourself alive....nothing special. It's not bad, just meh.
"But MoonKat, you just said the lore is part of the charm!" Here is where you need to know the difference between story and lore. When I say lore I refer to the world, when I say story I refer to your character's storyline. Audio logs in Doom 3? Lore. Cut Scenes where your character is spying on a conversation? Story. Wuppo's story is boring. Without spoiling anything it's basically a Wum learning to not be a giant♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥......meh.
Wuppo is not Game of the Year, it has some glaring issues that keep me from considering it a perfect experience.
What hat does what? Am I supposed to kill this thing? What's my objective exactly? What's the advantage of being fat versus not being fat? How do I sneak? Oh...I can go in some boxes but not others? Why do I need to whistle? There is so many more questions I could bring up but it would spoil some story elements. I am not complaining about challenge, I don't need a minimap or hand holding tutorials, but actually knowing what items do would be helpful. Some of the solutions to puzzles are almost impossible to solve by yourself. A spoiler-free-example is when a fisherman needs a hook, where do you get the hook? A store right? Of course! But wait, there is a bunch of hooks...which hook does he need? I bought the hook and he fished out an item that I need for what exactly? Some of the cryptic moments are fun, but majority of the time leave me with a guide open.
I have a Nvidia 1070 Graphics card with a current gen processor and this game still stutters from time to time on max graphic

Instead of typing out a long explaination I'm just going to give you an instance of where this drives me mad. You can only equip 1 item at one time. A candle is used for light and sits on your head. If equipped, you can't use your gun. There is some enemies in pitch black areas......bull$%!#....I hate that mechanic.
In the end...Wuppo is a game you should definately pick up for 5 bucks when it's on sale. You'll get a lot of amazing experiences out of this game. It's not perfect, but isn't bad, it's actually pretty good. If you want me to cover more areas of the game, let me know and I will update the review. Man, This game took me by storm after playing Episode 1.
I thought Sonic The Hedgehog Episode 2 was going to be boring like Episode 1, But I was wrong in typical game fasion.
I will go directly into everything and adding in a new part.
SPOLIERS/STORY: This start off with Sonic and Tails flying the Tornado and ended up landing where they notice Eggman is back at it *For the 15th time today* again! After clearing the first zone and moving on to the boss of the second zone, You realized 1st Tails is a idiot for leaving rockets all over the place and on another planet... 2nd Metal Sonic is back?! How did he survive you wondering, After leaving him destroyed on Little Planet *Refer to Sonic CD for more details.*
Quick Backstory: Remember Eggman base from Episode 1 Turns out he been using it to charge up Metal Sonic, And he been distracting you by fighting you with machines. That's explain why the machines look so familer.
Gameplay: This game have more features beside the Normal Combo Pack, You also get Tails. BUT TRUST ME Tails is useful in this game, I know shocker right? This game main focus was on Co-Op features I believe then the simple Lonely Hedgehog. You can get a friend or a stranger to play with you online or offline! There is 2 moves you can perform, Super Spindash *Not the actual name* which is faster then normal spindash and can destroy certain things. Then there is Tails Glide Ability, We both know what this do like in every game with tails... But at least this time Tails can carry sonic *Kinda*
This game feel much easier then the other game, Which make it easier to digest.
Level Design: This game took notes on what they did wrong in Episode 1 and added new levels that not stright up rip-offs! One thing I never explained in my last review was I highy disliked the level design, It felt so boring and sometimes very unforgiving... I'm glad they added new stages to play through.
Graphics/visual: This game running on a new engine *Pretty sure the same as Sonic Generation now* And boy oh boy does it look better. From lighting and water, And I feel less annoyed.

Sonic the Hedgehog 4 - Episode II is a great improvement over Episode I :
-The graphics are actually really good in this one. The levels and backgrounds are actually 3D models and not fricking pre-rendered graphics. All of the levels look really good, even though it looks like they reused some assets from Sonic Generations.
-The music is a lot better, it's not something I'd listen to on loop, but it actually feels like Sonic music. (Though some of the tracks are pretty much fan-service, see the theme for the roller coaster level which has some Twinkle Park notes at the end or the Stardust Speedway remix).
-The Zones and Bosses are actually original, they're not copy-pasted off the Classics (though they do take some inspiration, for example Sky Fortress being clearly based off Flying Battery).
-The combo moves are a nice mechanic and are pretty fun to use, even though they break the flow if you're trying to speed through a level, but they're not always necessary to progress, only some levels require them at certain moments.
-We also get some Metal Sonic boss battles, it's fan-service, but I'm always up for a race against the robot.
TL;DR : This game improves a lot on where Episode I went wrong, and it's actually a pretty fun game with good graphics, music and levels. If you're planning on buying either of the two Episodes, buy this one, you're much better off that way.

When I was younger I was a sonic fan and I own all Genesis/Megadrive, Mastersystem and Dreamcast Sonic games even today. My favorite game was Sonic 3 & Knuckles but sadly Sonic 4 is a HUGE disappointment.
The physics and controls are not the same as the previous games, they try to behave the same but they kinda... feel fake.
The combo moves are pretty much required to complete a stage, they aren't that bad but it's one of those tiny annoying things that force you to slow down since you're REQUIRED to use them to progress like it or not.
Level design on this one is between good-and-terrible, there's a part in Oil Desert Zone that is very unforgiving. This episode is clearly harder than Episode 1... sometimes way too hard like the last boss of the game.
Boss fights thankfully are not a reboot of any boss from early games so there's a bit of originality and creativity here but fighting them can actually become tedious of how long it takes to beat them.
Length of the game it's too short, yeah I know it's just 1 of 2 episodes, but that strategy was just to cash in on the same game twice.
Overall, this game wasn't clearly designed by the original team behind the previous games (I should appreciate more info about this).
* Well... Sonic? And Tails!
* Nice 3D visuals
* 2D Gameplay
* No cutscenes
* No new characters to fill yet more the Sonic universe.
* Team work combos, including a similar one that was in Sonic 3
* Original, strong and difficult bosses
* Fake physics & controls regarding the previous titles.
* Nothing significantly new in gameplay apart of the combos
* Too short, only 5+Special Zones, Sonic 2 has 11+Special
* Team work combos being REQUIRED to finish a stage
* Last boss is waaaay too dificult for a sonic game
If you want a modern sonic game that is good go get Sonic Generations instead.
PS: I don't dislike the game, I find it OKAY-ISH, but i can't really recommend it as a sequel to the old ones.

This game came as a surprise to me.  Got it in a bundle. Didn't expect anything, didn't know about it. What I ended up with, was one of the best games I've ever played in certain categories.
Wuppo offers an immersive single-player exploration "platformer" built over the course of 7 years.  Where your actions seem to matter, and the world feels alive.  I voted Wuppo for the "Suspension of Disbelief" Steam award, because despite the wild setting, I was totally drawn in.  Wanted to know more, see more of this world.  ... (It ended too soon!)
There's just a wealth of detail and interestingly executed ideas that you won't find in even the best games that sets this game apart.  Details rarely found in a 2D format.  And this is where the game succeeds the most imo. (Also fun for a wide range of ages I imagine.)
It also features some memorable use of music, the occasional but interesting battle, and plenty of secrets to uncover.  It's just a really good example of an indie game.  A two person crew spend 7 years creating a game, no kickstarter/crowdfunding.  And they made something special.
What can I say, but think about it!  It's currently 70% off and less than Undertale's soundtrack on sale.  I call that a good deal.
If you want some cons...?
Suprisingly I prefer mouse and keyboard for this game.
I admit I got stuck near the start by behaving unexpectedly.  Some things are not spoonfed, and I didn't realize I should shoot a certain object.
Single save spot per game.
Also, battles can be far and few, but unexpectedly difficult on normal near the end.
I wish the game was bigger...  Even though I got 30 hours out of it by exploring every corner without even restarting the game.
Oh and some achievements are tough without a guide.
PS - The only game that I would directly compare it to, would be the free game: Strawberry Jam, made by Daniel Remar (creator of games like Iji, Hyper Princess Pitch, Hero Core; part of Ludosity which created games like Ittle Dew, Princess Remedy), minus the battles.
A platformer with a wonderfully detailed, alive world to explore. Made me feel like a kid again :)

Black Ops 2 is the most underrated game in the franchise
Blops 2 tried to be different than the previous Call of Doodoos but did it succeed ? Yes!
The Singleplayer
So once again you play as an unstoppable killing machine. What makes this campaign stand out, however, is the fact that your actions and choices actually change the outcome of the game.
There are about 4 different endings. Each triggered by the choices/actions you make and or take.
There's also some little consequences that just scar some of your "teammates".
Having different endings in a FPS is a very rare thing. Let alone the fact that the ending depends on the actions you take.
In Deus Ex: Human Revolution your actions didn't matter at all. In the end you just chose between four different endings.
This is not the case in here. In here the ending depends on what you did on the road...making this story more dynamic and even beats some of the RPGs when it comes to affecting the world/story you're in. - Looking at you Mass Effect 3 and Skyrim - No matter what you do in these games, it doesn't matter. Yes, both are good games but you have no effect on the world or the story...yet they call themselves RPGs.
Call of Duty: Black Ops II created a good and dynamic campaign that should set a new par to all FPSs but unfortunatelly this little but important aspect of the game is overlooked just because "hurpdurr it's another CoD"...so what ? This CoD tried! Tried and succeeded!
The gameplay itself is your old-known CoD gameplay and we're glad that it's back! Admit it! If CoD would change their gameplay then there would be a lot of angry people out there.
Would you like CS to change the gameplay ? NO! People got angry at DICE when they made character movement more smooth in Battlefield...there's no pleasing people.
The character movement is, however, a bit smoother than in the previous CoDs and that makes the game a bit more enjoyable. Especially in the multiplayer.
The Multiplayer
I put around 150-160 hours into the multiplayer and I still have nothing to say about it...it's good.
So far i've only enjoyed 3 CoD multiplayers: CoD4, MW2 and Blops2.
So Blops 2 is in my top 3 Call of Duty games. - This is saying a lot! CoD4 and MW2 are considered the best CoD games even by the hardcore CoD haters!
The multiplayer in Blops2 is well balanced, gives you a lot of freedom (in class creation), makes it easier to record gameplay footages and is just simple fun.
The only issue i have, with the multiplayer, is that it uses matchmaking instead of having a simple server list.
It's still a very good multiplayer experience and i would recommend it to all kinds of FPS fans!
The game is definitely worth the full price. Only good CoD game on the market that's worth the full price!
+Different choices and endings add replay value to the 8-12h campaign making it a 16-48h campaign.
+Fun and balanced multiplayer that for the first time really lets you play the way YOU prefer.
+Co-op zombie modes
-No server list
You don't need to own any DLCs to fully enjoy this title

One of the biggest brothers in the trading and economic simulation genres, X3 Terran Conflict is, in my opinion, the go-to-game in the series over the vanilla X3 and Albion Prelude flavors (this is being written prior to the release of Reuinion).
X3 is a game that will worm its way into the hearts of those who enjoy the RPG mechanic of starting out small and building yourself up. No green slimes will be slain, though. In this game you'll be starting out in a modest little space fighter or freighter and working your way into power and prosperity through combat, trade, or a mix of the two (salvaging gear from the strife of others).
While combat was fun, and shouldn't dissapoint anyone coming from the Freespace school of gaming, I found trading and fleet management to be the most enjoyable and challenging parts of the game. X3's logistics, economy, and trading mechanics are as complex as they are fun, and a wonderful reward for those willing to brave the learning curve.

I recommend this game to all anal-retentive would-be galaxy empire overlords who blush at the mere mention of detail oriented micro management.  If building an interstellar commerce empire in realtime gives you a stiffy, then I ask, What are you waiting for?  Get X3!  It's the game that plays itself on your second, unused computer!

What is there to say about Prison Architect but wow! As a build-em-up, lock-em-up whatever-you-wanna-describe-it-as-em-up, this game has a lot of bases covered!
You're given a plot of land, you have some money and you're tasked with locking up some crims. The interface is as simple as you can get, if not infuriating at some points due to how close you have to zoom in to see items for a specific small room. The build can be as big or as small as you desire, tending to how hard you want the challenge to be. Keep it small with minimum security with few prisoners to break out, or make a mammoth prison with hundreds, if not thousands if you want that achievement, of prisoners. It's one of those very curious games that allows you to push it as far as you dare, then watch as it pushes you back as you desperately try to bring balance and order to an ever increasingly complicated organised mess.
If this doesn't float your boat, then there's always other peoples' prisons that have been shared that you can manage, or even as a new feature, break out of them! I find this incredibly entertaining, if just not got the complete hang of it yet.
The game isn't without its bugs though, and the developers are all too aware of them. So I'm sure there are loads of people eagerly awaiting the next update, whenever it is. For example, it seems very difficult to get prisoners to be assigned to a dormitory, as a cell with just 6 squares meets the criteria of an 18 square per person area when no-one's in it. Infuriating if not intreguing. Still, it's not as bad as the old bugs. They were just comical.
The art style is unique too. Perhaps the idea of floating bodies and heads are not everyone's cup of tea, but the simplicity of the people and their actions, a job is completed by waving an item at other items, sparks a whimsical laziness. Plus the idea one workman can move an entire water pump, a power station or wait at a cell door holding a bed is way too amusing.
But aside from all the special stuff, the game is very much a pleasure to play. No doubt people would say it becomes boring after a while and rather samey; perhaps it does, but it's one of those games that is what you make it. You could create the same prison a hundred times and have different people in it, each with different behaviour patterns and strengths.
If you like 2D, top down building games with whimsical people, animations and the occasional quirk, then it's well worth the intro price, if not more! Would recommend!

So Sonic 4: Ep.1 was a bit of a letdown condidering how much hype it got (you can go check out my ep.1 review as well). So SEGA a year and half later came out with Sonic The Hedgehog 4: Episode 2. Or in other words the LAST episode in the sonic 4 saga.
Well storywize. Sonic meets up with Tails and he says that little planet from Sonic CD would be making its annual return. But Sonic scences that Eggman is once again up to no good and they hop in the tornado and go see the commotion. Well Little Planet this time decided to be a) much larger and b) appear in space this time. Suddenly they run into Metal Sonic. Why is he here? Its explained later. After taking down Eggmans flying ship he reveals that he used little planet as the bases for his new base the Death Egg MK.2. After taking down Metal Sonic and destroying the heart Sonic and Tails barely escape the death egg and..... thats it. What the ♥♥♥♥ was that? The death egg remains intact, little planet is still trapped inside and we still dont know how metal sonic got there? What kind of♥♥♥♥♥♥id That?
Okay gameplay. So Sonic now has Tails follow him around the stages and by pressing the X button they can do a co-op move that depends were you activate it in the air or underwater Tails carrys sonic to safety and on the ground they charge up a super spin dash and obliterate enemies. I tgink this is a pretty cool idea. But you can decide which character is the lead. You always play as Sonic, not my idea why cant I play as tails? Sonic can still do all the things he can do in Ep.1 but the physics have been improved tremondously over ep.1 and rolling is now a good use in means of gaining speed as well. we even get some creative uses of the homing attack instead of just enemie chains (which there is also much less of them as well). There are still a fair amout of speed boosters but definitely less than ep.1. The stages themself are much more orifional that ep.1 so we Have Slyvania Castle Zone, White Park Zone, NOT-Oil Ocean Zone (Oil Desert Zone) and NOT-Wing Fortress Zone (Sky Fortrress Zone). Like ep.1 while some level themes may be reused the level design is differnt. The level design definitely feels less barren that ep.1, still a bit rough around the edges but nothing ill lose sleep over. Well what about those special stages? Well like ep.1 if you collect 50 rings and jump into the ring at the end you'll be transported to the special stage. The special stages are similer to the sonic 2, Sonic Pocket adveture, Sonic Ruch and Sonic Colours DS as you run along a halfpipe and collect a certen amout of rings. Get enought you get a chaos emerald and you can play as super sonic in regular stages withc is always nice. In terms of bosses well this is the games weakness... when your not fighting eggman your fighting metal sonic. Eggmans bosses, while origonal, are bad. They overstay their welcome by about 3 minuits and the looping 6 times per minuite music doesnt help. The metal sonic fight are thankfully much better, expecialy the white park boss I always get a kik out of that. as I said before all the bosses in this game are origonal apart from the 4th and final encounter with metal sonic being a remake of the race from Sonic CD. The finlal boss is at best ok, but I just wish there was more to it.
In terms of looks, this game excells. While i dont mind how ep.1 looks, but this is soo much better and the result is one fantastic looking game. Music is better than ep.1, but some of the tracks can still be repetetive as hell and some just sound bad like oil deserts act 2 and act 3 music. The game, belive it or not, also has local and online multiplayer were ojne of you controls sonic and the other Tails. I havent triend it myself coz no one plays this game much anymore but if playing this game with a friend or online appears to you then by all means do so. There are also red rings to collect in the stages but iunless your an achevement lover then don't bother as you don't need to collect then to prroceed and they dont unlock anything extra. The ♥♥♥♥?
Also if you have both Ep. 1 and Ep.2 on the some system you get a special 'lock on' extra in the form of Episode Metal. You play as Metal sonic (he controls exactly the same btw) through 4 of the stages from ep.1 and it explains how metal sonic returned from Sonic CD. Its nothing special at all and it should only take you about 15 minuits to finish. So basicly Eggman by the power of pointing powers up Metal Sonic and by being rebuilt in Mad Gear and absorbing some purple void in lost labyrinth zone hes fully restores and he flies off and meets Sonic and Tails in white park. Huzzar???
Well Sonic 4: Episode 2 in my opinion is a much better game when conpaired to Episode 1. Better graphics, better physicls, cirtenly better level design and overall is a much more enjoyable experience. At £9.99 i do think that is asking maybe a bit much for this game and I do wish the bosses were better and their be less springs and speed boosters but if you want a light hearted sonic game then go for it.

The third Batman game was created by a developer other than Rocksteady and many gamers will affirm that the title suffers for it but I actually think it's quite the opposite.  With a new developer and a game that occurs prior to the first Batman title we get to see an interesting, new side of the Caped Crusader: the young, yet not overwhelmingly inexperienced Detective.  The developers not only brought a substantially refreshed rogues gallery and collection of art assets but also new interpretations/views to the Batman universe.  Additionally, we get to finally see Batman as the up-and-coming Dark Knight: a foe to be feared and reckoned with.  Despite introducing us to a Dark Knight that has limited experience and city-wide cache, the game doesn't present a rookie story at all in fact, as Batman has all his finalized gear and resources to bear on enemies.  In fact, he's been able to effectively thwart several enemies and has already begun to generate a fearsome reputation.  In short, we get a Batman that has the best of both worlds at a point in his crimefighting career where he begins to gain critical mass but wherein everything is still exciting and new.
The combat, movement and gameplay are all that you would expect from previous titles.  You still utilize a combination of combat, trickery and subterfuge to accomplish objectives.  And while the story is interesting at first ( you are being hunted by a rogues gallery of villains), the title is quickly spoiled by the introduction of a cliched and overused concept character that overwhelms most of the series.  In this way, I would have preferred dealing with many of the villains individually, through the utilization of cleverness, open gameplay and legitimate cognitive gymnastics rather than the same overused rote tropes from the three sequels.  I believe that its this similarity to the sequels that makes Arkham Origins suffer more than anything itself.  Combat is fun and interesting at first but can grind a bit as you punch and sock your way thorugh a parade of *thousands* of goons(literally), in a wave of pointlessness that never truly abates.  Much like Arkham City, you are plunged into a city with often a few too many options and dangling plotlines.
The combat against some of the rogues gallery is new, fresh and even comical however and unlike Arkham City, you are able to appreciate the boss battles at bit more pointedly in this go-around.  The Deathstroke boss battle was a  personal favorite of mine which on occasion felt like a legitimate fight between the young Caped Crusader and the ultimate Assassin.  While the fight was a little repetitious and the ending may seem far-fetched, it at least tried to do something previous Rocksteady Batman games didn't do: have him battle ONE opponent.  Deathstroke was the only thing you had to worry about during the fight and he was more than enough.  The game developers didn't feel like they had to cheat by spawning waves of goons and turbogoons to "sweeten" and "intensify the boss fight.  And for that, I am thankful since it feels different from previous Batman game villains.
While the story suffers at spots and the ending doesn't exactly have epic implications for the Batman mythos, Batman: Arkham Origins is an attractive, fluid game that, once fully patched, is a capable successor to the Rocksteady pantheon of Batman games.  It's *definitely* better than the abomination that Rocksteady released a few scant years later.  This game isn't an amazing title but it's at least as good as Arkham City and maybe close to Arkham Asylum.
If you can find it on sale for 8 dollars or less, you should pick it up.

You're given a plot of land, you have some money and you're tasked with locking up some crims. The interface is as simple as you can get, if not infuriating at some points due to how close you have to zoom in to see items for a specific small room. The build can be as big or as small as you desire, tending to how hard you want the challenge to be. Keep it small with minimum security with few prisoners to break out, or make a mammoth prison with hundreds, if not thousands if you want that achievement, of prisoners. It's one of those very curious games that allows you to push it as far as you dare, then watch as it pushes you back as you desperately try to bring balance and order to an ever increasingly complicated organised mess.
If this doesn't float your boat, then there's always other peoples' prisons that have been shared that you can manage, or even as a new feature, break out of them! I find this incredibly entertaining, if just not got the complete hang of it yet.
The game isn't without its bugs though, and the developers are all too aware of them. So I'm sure there are loads of people eagerly awaiting the next update, whenever it is. For example, it seems very difficult to get prisoners to be assigned to a dormitory, as a cell with just 6 squares meets the criteria of an 18 square per person area when no-one's in it. Infuriating if not intreguing. Still, it's not as bad as the old bugs. They were just comical.
The art style is unique too. Perhaps the idea of floating bodies and heads are not everyone's cup of tea, but the simplicity of the people and their actions, a job is completed by waving an item at other items, sparks a whimsical laziness. Plus the idea one workman can move an entire water pump, a power station or wait at a cell door holding a bed is way too amusing.
But aside from all the special stuff, the game is very much a pleasure to play. No doubt people would say it becomes boring after a while and rather samey; perhaps it does, but it's one of those games that is what you make it. You could create the same prison a hundred times and have different people in it, each with different behaviour patterns and strengths.
If you like 2D, top down building games with whimsical people, animations and the occasional quirk, then it's well worth the intro price, if not more! Would recommend!

First and foremost I would like to reiterate, what 99% of players before me have stated - that this is an aesthetically STUNNING game. The storyline is also extremely strong in my opinion, with a soundtrack and intermittent cutscenes that really adds some wonderful depth to the small list of characters and the story.
In terms of the game's mechanics, learning how to time your different moves is tricky at first, and I will admit I got frustrated enough once during my time of playing Ori and the Blind Forest that I quit the game.... Only to find myself opening the game right back up again not five minutes later because that's how much it draws you in. You do eventually learn how to do everything to a T, but it does take practice, and the game allows for you to hone these skills before they are critical to continuing the story.
For this reason I would not advice you to buy this game if you're wanting something relaxing to play - it takes a lot of effort. But for anyone who loves beautiful, moving games, that also come with challenges, in terms of both skill and puzzle solving, then ABSOLUTELY
. It left me both speechless, and completely satisified by the end, and someone even started cutting onions close by. It's also the kind of game that has a *bit* of replayability if you want to get those rarer achievements!
In terms of bugs and glitches, I found none.
My experience of the game:
I enjoy these kinds of games for their stories most of all (although I also freaking love mini-puzzles!) and thus I played on easy mode. That still left plenty of challenges, especially as I made a point of exploring every inch of the map and collecting every single pick-up (called cells) there was. Yes, running back and forth as I discovered the locations of more and more cells did grow a little tedious, but the thing to remember is that it's not necessary to continuing the game and I did it by choice - although it proved very useful to have the extra life and energy sitting around for the final area of the map.
Collecting all of those pick-ups resulted in my game lasting 11 and a half hours, completed over three days. If I hadn't gone the extra mile to get those extra achievements I expect the game would have taken about 10 hours.

Overall, it's an ok platformer (not great, but enjoyable enough to recommend it), it's very short but it's worth its prince on sale
It contains 9 levels plus 3 bosses through 3 thematic worlds. Most of the content it's very easy (with the exception of the last level and the last boss), but you can replay the levels finding better scores and I think get good scores on the levels can be more challenging.
Don't expect something as polished as Sonic Generations or Freedom Planet.

The level design is poor. They force team mechanics onto you, and limit your options. Throughout the entire game, they expect you to use team powers (use Tails to fly, or use Tails for a super spin dash) to get through certain sections. Using these abilities takes you out of Super Sonic, and it just hinders the flow overall.
Boss fights weren't fun for me. Certain boss fights are designed around the team mechanics as well. They split the boss bights into their own separate stages. You can't rack up rings to completely destroy the bosses, and instead... they only give you ~50 rings to fight them. I didn't kill any boss with the 50 rings they gave, and had to finish the fight as normal sonic. My favourite aspect of the classic titles was to destroy the game as super/hyper sonic, despite the little challenge that posed. It was a power fantasy, and this game has virtually none of that.
I'd suggest just getting Sonic 3 & Knuckles. It has more content than this one (Knuckles, Hyper Sonic, Checkpoint mini-games, Electric shields, Fire shields), the levels are designed to allow for more experimentation, and the bosses generally allow for more approaches.

Absolutely get this game if you like beat-em ups or hack and slashes. Many people instantly hated this game when it came out because *gasp Dante's hair wasn't white. According to Wikipedia DmC: Devil May Cry (DMC) takes place in an alternate universe. So it is like comic book adaptations. Christopher Nolan's Batman is not the same Batman in the Arkham games or the the animated series. I have never played a Devil May Cry game before so I do not come from the same boat as those people. Anyways about the game...
Story:
Dante, a half demon half angel humanoid, is almost assassinated by Mundus, the Demon King. Mundus poses as a human and controls the world through financial means with his giant corporation or something. He also has propaganda with a Fox News like anchor and he keeps the people docile with a popular Mountain Dew looking soft drink.  He escapes his assassination attempt with the help of Kat, a human medium who knows some witchcraft. She takes him to see his brother Vergil who looks like a hipster. Vergil is the masked leader of an organization that is rebelling against Mundus. Dante is reluctant to join but later does when he finds out that Mundus killed his mother and imprisoned his father. He mostly cares for his mother since he hates "demon scum". So they set out on an adventurous quest to kill Mundus by killing the Fox News anchor and stopping the supply of Mountain Dew.
Dante is a funny guy. He cusses alot and is sarcastic. In one scene he has to get in a nightclub. The bouncer says with a smile "You're not on the list.” Dante then punches him, grabs his list, writes "♥♥♥♥ You!" and says I am now. He is kind of like Duke Nukem because he also sleeps with strippers in his spare time (I don't know where he gets the money).
Kat is a spiritual medium who can get Dante and Vergil in and out of Limbo: the demon world. She eventually
Before the game she is rescued by Vergil after he shows her how demons control the world.
Vergil is an “Anonymous” like rebel who seeks to destroy the Demon King Mundus. If I say anymore I will spoil the game. Do not look at the achievements if you don’t want the game spoiled.
Gameplay:
You have 4 types of weapons: regular, heavy, light, and guns. By default the XYAB buttons will let you use your default weapon. If you hold RT you can use your heavy weapon with the XYAB buttons. If you hold LT you can use the Light weapons. X by default lets you use the guns. You get 2 types of Light and Heavy weapons and 3 types of guns. Each light and heavy weapon is useful for certain situations and some enemies can only be killed with a certain type of weapon. I never found myself using the guns too much. They do little damage and using your swords is best in my opinion. Although the shotgun useful for destroying certain projectiles. You don't get all of these weapons at the start. You slowly get them as the story progresses. If you get a new weapon it doesn't necessarily mean it’s better than the last one. For example the rebellion has the Trillion Stabs ability which is great for wearing down an enemy at your mercy while the Gauntlets are useful for bigger slower enemies (since it is a slow weapon). It is good to experiment with them.
Anyone can pick up this game but pros can master it. Either way you will have alot of fun with this game. The setting is great and there is a good variety of enemies and a great arsenal for you to use against them. The game is fairly long with 20 levels and the final boss is epic and satisfying. There are some platforming elements but they are not annoying and abundant like Guacameele. It is definitely a game you should not miss out on unless you are demon scum.

I'll collect so much data, gain such a deep understanding of cancer, and hammer so much information in my brian, that my mind will instantly formulate a cure just by looking at a single cancer cell in the microscope. This will be the biggest breakthrough of humanity! One of the biggest enemies of mankind has been defeated! The whole world shall celebrate! But not me. Not yet.
My work is not yet done.
The research goes on. Soon cancer will become a simple disease you can cure as easily as a flu, you'll get a simple pill in the local drug store and BAM! All is well again, the cancer cells die and get replaced by healthy ones. Cancer is something of the past. So what good is it to be a researcher of cancer now? Either way, the research must go on. It can't stop. It's not over yet.
After a few years, a new type of mutation, completely immune to the current medicine, is discovered. It kills millions around the world. It takes 10 years until a definitive cure for this new type of cancer is devised.
That mutation, I named Super Meat Boy. Just so I could say I have finally rid the world of this cancer.
And so I look around me. I'm old, weak, and lying in my bed. It's not long for me now. I begin pondering on my life. I recall all the choices I had made. Was it really worth it, to dedicate the entirety of my life just to show my displease with a game I played when I was young? It was actually a pretty good game, so all of this was fueled by my own short temper. If I went back to that day, would I still choose this same path?
I reach around to the side, open a drawer and from it I take an old picture frame, showing severe signs of aging and physical abuse. It depicts the development team of this game.
"Hell ♥♥♥♥ing yes, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s!" I say as I give the frame the middle finger. I fling across the room, and as it shatters against the wall, I take my last breath.
...
I... wake up? I see a group of men speaking what seems like English but with a heavy accent. Oh, that's right. I kind of expected humanity to eventually do this. To somehow revive the minds of people that did great deeds for mankind. It's a bit more sophisticated than I had expected. It seems they were able to upload my brain into an artificial biological body. Pretty much, it means I live again. One of the scientists explains to me that first I need to run a bunch of tests to ensure I get used to my new body, and that my mind works as expected. Two weeks of tests goes by. On the 17th day of testing, it's time to test my mind reaction, spatial perception and time perception. The scientist explains to me that I will have to play a game from their time. It's a simple 16-bit platformer said to be pretty hardcore.

Heartwarming, unique adventure hidden behind silly presentation and relative lack of popularity - Wuppo delivers an amazing world, interactivity and genre mashup that screams
You are a wum. The wuzziest, roundest and possibly laziest wum in the entire Wumhouse. So lazy, that you are a constant nuisance to the Wumhouse's main manager. When you spill your daily dose of ice cream all over the corridor, manager loses it and orders security to throw you over your room's balcony into the garden. After you lose few pounds when somebody steals the TV out of you (which you apparently ate previously) the new quest awaits for you - the search for a new home, happiness and your own little place in the world.
And what a world it is! Don't dismiss this game by its child-like graphics! The biggest draw of Wuppo is it's extremely cohesive, vibrant and unique world to explore and experience. Game goes lengths and miles to deliver locations and places that allow you to breathe in the atmosphere. Areas are not only large and visually distinct, but they are also filled to the brim with NPCs, interactive elements and details.
Streets, cities and homes are full of with creatures which seemingly have lives on their own, trams and trains have their own timetables that are real time and not only for show, amusement park rides have their waiting lines that you need to endure, cities have council meetings you can participate in... This game reminded me of Shenmue of all things! Yes, Wuppo doesn't go to such lengths as the Dreamcast classic, but the attention to detail and player interaction make for one of the most inviting and entrancing game worlds in my recent memory... and
.
Game world also greatly benefits from the fact that Wuppo heavily rewards you for careful exploration, helping other people along your journey and being generally a good person. Thanks to that, player agency is high and time spent roaming through all the attractions was enjoyable, happy-go-lucky experience, especially when the dialogue and humor is quite good here all across the board and plot kept going naturally at reasonable pace.
Another unique aspect of Wuppo, is that it doesn't label itself as a particular 2D platformer. Game world is semi-open, seamless and expansive, but it lacks upgrades, doors and interconnectivity of metroidvania. There are bosses and combat, but it's quite simplistic and most of the time you will out of the danger in secure, inhabited areas. There are some small puzzle elements, but this game cannot be called a puzzle-platformer either. This perplexing mix is hard to categorize, but works out very well, despite some wonkiness here and there. I need the commend developers that they sticked to their own breed of 2D platforming game and didn't make another washed out metroidvania. This makes Wuppo
and not only a set of doors to open sequentially.
Unfortunately, this is a place I need to drop some negatives, because there are a few to speak off. My few first moments into the game weren't so great, because I had a quite difficult time adjusting to the control scheme and inventory management. I played on gamepad and constant visits at inventory screen, to shuffle through the countless items wasn’t very comfortable and felt sometimes pace ruining even further down the line (especially in action sections). You can set up a quick-selections and overall you can get used to the control scheme (which default sets jumps on
of all places), but first hour was pretty difficult for me to grasp. You need to keep that in mind.
In addition, while I praised the mix of the gameplay mechanics, not everything gels in 100%. I found the default running and gunning lacking a bit of the punch and many puzzles in the areas felt a bit that they escaped from the classic adventure games with some noticeable obtusiveness. Fortunately, since the exploration is the main focus of the game, those problems aren't the dealbreakers, but Wuppo probably won't satisfy more mechanically oriented gamers that would like more snappy combat and/or more puzzle focus.
Take everything I mentioned, add a quite expansive and lovely soundtrack that I consider buying and sincere plot full of silly lore and you get everything to make your final purchasing decision. For me, Wuppo isn't an ideal or exceptionally amazing game, but it remains remarkably unique, full of charm and rare quirks that makes it difficult not to recommend for the asking price, especially if you want to play something really different. You could beat the game in around 7-8 hours, but I personally spent twice of that. I will leave the game quite satisfied and I hope that you will also enjoy your stay...

I will update this review when I have completed the game to talk about it's gameplay. For now, I've only played a little bit and I'll be talking about it's PC compatibility.
When I first played Sonic the Hedgehog Episode I on my laptop, nothing would work. No matter what software I downloaded, no matter how many times I verified the game cache, no matter how many times I updated Windows, and even after the multiple times uninstalled and reinstalled the game, it would not work. After two weeks of sadness and hatred towards Sega, I uninstalled and reinstalled the game one more time and it finally worked for no reason known to me. Because of this struggle, I was very skeptical of Sonic the Hedgehog 4 Episode II's PC compatibility. But I was far from disapointed.
When the game is first setup, it automatically looks for what required software such as DirectX you do and do not have on your computer, and immediately installs what you do not have. This potentially saved me weeks of stress and pain over the game not working if I were to not already have everythin necessary.  It has a pretty low default resolution for the game (300 x 200), and I was afraid that the graphics would either be ugly or the game would run slow. Fortunately, even at high resolution (1208 x 1024), it ran at a smooth 60 fps and this time the graphics looked like Sega actually tried this time. Instead of trying to have the graphics of Sonic the Hedgehog 1 in HD, this game instead had apporximately the graphics of Sonic Generations, only zoomed out. It wasn't like I have an impressive intel core i7 processor of 4.7 GHz, either. My processor is a intel core i3 of 2.1 GHz and it ran this game fine. So if you're afraid of this game because the last one didn't work or hard ugly graphics, don't be. So far this seems like a true Sega game. I have played a level or two and everything runs like a horse. The level design was very nostalgic and stayed true to Sonic.

First and foremost I would like to reiterate, what 99% of players before me have stated - that this is an aesthetically STUNNING game. The storyline is also extremely strong in my opinion, with a soundtrack and intermittent cutscenes that really adds some wonderful depth to the small list of characters and the story.
In terms of the game's mechanics, learning how to time your different moves is tricky at first, and I will admit I got frustrated enough once during my time of playing Ori and the Blind Forest that I quit the game.... Only to find myself opening the game right back up again not five minutes later because that's how much it draws you in. You do eventually learn how to do everything to a T, but it does take practice, and the game allows for you to hone these skills before they are critical to continuing the story.
For this reason I would not advice you to buy this game if you're wanting something relaxing to play - it takes a lot of effort. But for anyone who loves beautiful, moving games, that also come with challenges, in terms of both skill and puzzle solving, then ABSOLUTELY
. It left me both speechless, and completely satisified by the end, and someone even started cutting onions close by. It's also the kind of game that has a *bit* of replayability if you want to get those rarer achievements!
In terms of bugs and glitches, I found none.
My experience of the game:
I enjoy these kinds of games for their stories most of all (although I also freaking love mini-puzzles!) and thus I played on easy mode. That still left plenty of challenges, especially as I made a point of exploring every inch of the map and collecting every single pick-up (called cells) there was. Yes, running back and forth as I discovered the locations of more and more cells did grow a little tedious, but the thing to remember is that it's not necessary to continuing the game and I did it by choice - although it proved very useful to have the extra life and energy sitting around for the final area of the map.
Collecting all of those pick-ups resulted in my game lasting 11 and a half hours, completed over three days. If I hadn't gone the extra mile to get those extra achievements I expect the game would have taken about 10 hours.
TL:DR

The counters still don't work properly, and I would say they probably work even less of the time. It's very frustrating to die even though you pressed right mouse to block. Sometimes, other moves don't work right either. For instance, my aoe glue grenade never triggered despite buying the upgrade. The ground knockdown, a VERY important part of the game, worked probably only 90% of the time. I could probably think of a few more specifics, but the point is the controls are borked. It's probably because this is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ PC port, a fact that is evident in the menu layout and controls as well.
Another huge problem is the glitches. This game glitches SOOOO much, whether it's character models and cutscenes becoming pixelated, gliding animations spazzing out, or enemies getting stuck on corners. I even had some problems with side quests where they couldn't trigger or were uncompletable for some reason or another. Overall, this is a shoddy excuse for a game.
My last complaint has to do with the boss fights. The game sets up the story being about these  assassins who Black Mask hires to take you out: Deathstroke, Deadshot, Shiva, Firefly, Bane, Electrocutioner, and Copperhead. I was super excited to go up against these characters because they represented a new experience: characters that haven't appeared in the Arkham games before. However, Joker kind of hijacks the story halfway through and reveals he was Black Mask all along. The game becomes about taking down Joker instead of doing the assassins, and it turns out that Shiva and Deadshot aren't in there at all! Meanwhile, you have to fight Bane a total of three times, two of which are literally the exact same! It would have been much more fun to take down Black Mask and the assassins instead of Joker and hordes of thugs, which we've already done ad nauseam in the other Arkham games.
Seems to me that they changed writers or lost some budget halfway through.
All in all I expected a new experience, and really didn't get it. A few moments were interesting and unique, but most of it felt played out, medicore, and repetitive.

If you're reading this because you got burned by Mighty Number 9--here's your aloe vera. If you aren't--here's the Mega Man X Roguelite you didn't know you needed.
Controls and movement are spot-on, the powerups feel good (though I think they could use just a little more mechanical variety, rather than mostly stat tweaking), and the bosses are genuinely challenging. Difficulty ramp is very cleverly done--stages and boss rooms start having ever more sinister traps, and enemy combinations become more and more tricky to deal with. Even if you end up revisiting the same stage multiple times in the same run, it will feel noticeably more hostile each time.
I wasn't sure about the art style at first, but it grew on me--the player character animations are actually really nice, too. I think the bosses, and maybe a couple of enemies, could use another pass to make them a tad less goofy, though. Sound design is solid, and the soundtrack is excellent, though it harkens more to classic Mega Man than X.
Point is--it knows how to be fun, which is more than... some other games. You won't regret it.

I think this is actually a great entry in the Arkham series.
Everyone ♥♥♥♥♥ on this game because it's not made by Rocksteady (Developers of Arkham Asylum, City and Knight) but I don't see the problem with it, it's a pretty awesome game.
Pros
-Batman
-Freeflow combat rocks, it's so good yet simple, many games tried to mimic the Arkham mechanics (Like TASM2) but can't quite get it right.
-Stealth mechanics.
-Big Open world to explore full of criminals.
-Interesting story with surprising twists.
-Full of neat easter eggs and amazing attention to detail.
-Amazing voice acting
-Lots of content: costumes, side missions, challenge maps and even Deathstroke as a playable character!
-Online mode
Cons
-There are quite a number of bugs, I remember that the first time I got into the Batcave I got stuck near the Computer and Batman kept walking in a loop (Yeaaah, a glitch that forced me to reset the game on the first 15 minutes is not a good sign)
-Sometimes the controls can be a bit awqward, in some occasions I wanted to counter the enemy's attack but for some reason Batman took out the disruptor, it can be pretty damn annoying when you get a great combo and it's all gone because the game messes up.
-Sometimes the enemy variety is not right. Fighting two enemy types at the same time? Alright. But fighting a guy with venom, a freaking armored criminal, some guys with guns...It's extremely difficult to keep the combos going and it's a stupid way to make the game harder.
I love the game, it does have some flaws but they are really minor ones and I still think it's a worthy sequel (Or prequel, whatever) to Arkham City. Not only a fantastic Batman game, but one damn awesome Action game in general.

The gameplay is very challenging and precise, mostly based on exploration, with difficult platforming sections everywhere. The gameplay, story and environment all feel like one organic creation, rather than multiple separate components. Your progression in the story is reflected by changes in mechanics and environments.
I could ramble on forever about how stunning this game is, but I have to stop somewhere, so to conclude, I highly recommend this game to anyone that doesn't hate platformers.

I rate this game 8/10.
Some of the good:
The predator/stealth stuff is my favorite. Using the remote claw to connect two vantage points together to walk on was a nice feature; it gives me more mobility to stalk enemies to perform a quick takedown and then use it to fly away.
Some of the bad:

The ugly:
There were a few times when the glitches/bugs caused me to unable to finish a quest or go into the next area because a criminal was stuck in a wall. I was able to use the restart feature to fix this, but I shouldn't have to do that. Also, the multiplayer option here is no longer accessible. The game developer should have stated this somewhere for consumers to know before buying the game. I was looking forward to playing online to test my stealth skills against human players, but online play is dead. It's a cute little turn based RPG with a charming story involving robots that have just enough AI as to exude personality in the way WALL-E's robot characters did.  The fighting moves have just enough variation, and anyone that's played a JRPG in the last 20 years will have no trouble identifying the "physical," "magical" and "AoE" moves.  There are some places where you can choose to grind up character stats by revisiting enemies in cyberspace if needed, but you also seem to be able to pursue the story without being gated.  The "maze" of the ship and platforming are interesting without being overwhelming.  The combat has a bit of a Shadowrun inspired feel to it which will make you grin with nostalgia.
For a cheap little indie RPG it's fun.  It's not going to blow your mind, but for a casual time waster it does the job splendidly, hearkening back to simpler times.  Sometimes you just need a break from modern real time RPGs that require 100% of your focus and engagement, and this game understands that.

This game is good, maybe even very good but its just about the most maximalist thing going.
It feels like the result of a brainstorming session where someone asked "what do people like in indie games these games?" and the answer came as "feelings" so the studio wanted to compete by making a game with the most feelings ever. The most emotions possible. That's good value for money, innit? So you're going to get beaten over the head with all the emotions you could ever want, and get your heartstrings tugged every second that you're playing the game. The music is constantly jerking from triumphant and epic to saccharine and cloying to creepy and sad, and the visuals look like someone dropped a piano on Thomas Kinkade's head and he woke up thinking that he was Hieronymus Bosch. All teals and orange, red and blue, purple and green. It doesn't look great. It looks impressive, sure but not great exactly. As a result the game isn't very effective when it comes to being a moving experience - no downtime between the audio bombast and spectacular visuals means there is not much in the way of atmosphere being established (compare and contrast with Axiom Verge and Hollow Knight). Worse - big owl aside, the characters couldn't be more generically cute if they were designed by algorithm, looking like Pixar creations that literally have their edges sanded down. Thumbs down for both atmosphere and personality, because it as far as I'm concerned it has neither.
What appealed to me initially is that this wasn't yet another pixel art thing, but it ended up convincing me that the pixel art or simple style of most other 2D indie titles is more of a necessity than it may seem. Ori is presented like an exploration, metroidy, castlevaniay, experience but it really isn't - its more like Super Meat Boy with some optional backtracking, with obligatory frustrating memory test sequences. This is a problem because the precision platforming clashes horribly with the technicolour blob-puke of the visuals and even though the platforming is decent, its horribly confusing to my terrible aging eyes and it doesn't help that the main character has an identical blob orbitting it at all times. The big, simple style of Guacamelee was more appropriate here even if Ori's mechanics are tigher and more fun to use.
In general, the mechanics are all pretty fun and satisfying. The save gimmick is great, although its not really suited to exploration and works best when the game is a linear "dying is fun" kind of experience. Bouncing off projectiles would be very fun indeed if the game didn't look like a kaleidoscope full of half-digested Lucky Charms™ and I could see what I was doing. But much like everything else, this game goes all out with mechanics and gives you loads of them plus a totally vestigial levelling system which you barely need to use at all. So you can ponder the needlessly huge skill tree while the "ethnic winds" (as the credit sequence calls them ) of the soundtrack try to make you feel like the teariest sadboy in gamerland.
Conclusion: It's fine but Good Lord I'm Getting Old, Videogames. Stop Trying To Say Too Many Things At Once. Calm Down.

Sharing in the same feeling of a lot of people who play Euro Truck Simulator 2, I honestly don't know why I enjoy playing this game, nor do I know why I enjoyed playing ETS1 either. It isn't the most pretty, the most feature-packed, and it definitely isn't the most exciting. But there's something about taking a long drive down open roads, listening to your favourite music, louding honking and swearing at the other drivers on the road as you come to a violent stop.
ETS2 has quite a few problems, mainly in the AI drivers and the traffic offence system. Part of my reason for want to write this review at 17 hours playtime, is due to my very recent experience taking 22,000kg of live ammunition from London to Grimsby. I had just gotten into Grimsby, driving at a comfortable 45km as a bus pulled right out in front of me, dealing 13% damage to my truck (about $10,000 worth) and 2% damage to my cargo. And I still got the ticket for it.
That aside, the very obvious speed traps are a little annoying. Sometimes the speed limit in areas affected by road works goes from 48km to 97km for a few kilometres and then back down to 48km. The fatigue indicatior is a little hard to read, as the blue bleeds into the grey a little. But these are minor nitpicks.
I'd personally recommend this game, as it is quite relaxing when everything is going well. The world isn't as populated as some people may like, I wish there were more areas to explore. But the game competently does what it says on the tin, and if that's what you'd like, then you'll like this.
There's also multiplayer for those interested. Haven't tried it personally, so I don't have an opinion.
